Customers are developers, builders and contractors, and revenue comes from building system sales and design services. It raised a large venture round in 2021. A B2B construction-tech firm with little consumer brand awareness and no sports-marketing profile.

Salary Finance is a London-based financial wellbeing provider that partners with employers to offer their staff affordable loans repaid through payroll deduction, plus savings accounts and financial education tools. Employees at participating firms apply through a digital platform, the employer offers it as a benefit, and Salary Finance earns interest on the loans. Founded in 2015, it has served large UK employers including NHS trusts and major retailers, and expanded into the US. It raised significant institutional investment, including a round in 2021. Consumer awareness is mostly through employers rather than advertising.

System One is a US professional staffing and workforce solutions firm headquartered in Pittsburgh, supplying contract, direct-hire and managed-service talent in engineering, IT, scientific, clinical, finance and skilled-trades roles. Customers are large corporations in industries such as energy, life sciences, aerospace, technology and manufacturing, and revenue is the markup on placed workers' hours. It has grown through acquisitions, including Ablest and Mountain, and has revenue well above 1 billion dollars with thousands of staff. It is privately held with private equity backing. B2B brand with moderate recognition in the staffing industry and little consumer profile.

Cardone Capital is a real estate investment firm founded by sales trainer and entrepreneur Grant Cardone, based in Aventura, Florida. It raises money from accredited and, later, retail investors through private funds and crowdfunding, buying large multifamily apartment communities in the US Sun Belt, with a portfolio of billions of dollars in assets under management. Revenue comes from fees and property income, and investors receive distributions. The firm draws strong brand awareness from Grant Cardone's heavy social media and TV presence, giving it unusually high marketing spend for a property investor.

E-House (China) is a Chinese real estate services company that began as a residential property agency and brokerage, offering primary-market sales agency, consulting, online platforms and property data to developers and homebuyers. It built the CRIC real estate data and research platform, and was listed on the NYSE (EJ) in 2007 before going private in 2016. It later expanded into property management and online services. Its customers are developers and buyers across many Chinese cities. Brand is well known in the Chinese property trade, but not an international consumer name.

Eranove is a French-headquartered utility group that operates electricity generation and water production and distribution in Africa. Its key operations include the SODECI water utility and CIE electricity utility in Côte d'Ivoire, and water operations in Senegal and Gabon, plus development of solar and hydro projects. Customers are households and industries billed through concession and licence arrangements. Ownership includes private infrastructure investors alongside African institutional partners. Based in Puteaux near Paris. B2B and concession-type brand, with local consumer recognition in West Africa only.

Hetao101 is a Chinese online education company in Beijing offering programming and computer science courses for children, such as Scratch, Python and competition-style coding, delivered through live online classes with tutors. Parents pay course fees. It grew quickly during the 2020-2021 online education boom, backed by Chinese venture investors, and is one of the larger coding-for-kids names in China. The 2021 regulatory tightening on tutoring mostly targeted school subjects, so coding classes were less affected. Known to Chinese parents but with little awareness abroad.

Incode Technologies is a San Francisco-based identity verification and authentication company, founded in 2015 by Ricardo Amper, which supplies AI-based face recognition, document verification and fraud prevention software used for customer onboarding and login. Customers include banks, fintechs, telecoms, airlines and governments, and it also offers a biometric identity wallet. Revenue comes from per-transaction and subscription fees. It has a major presence in Latin America and the US and serves large financial institutions. B2B product, with consumers meeting it only when verifying identity, so brand awareness is low outside the industry.

Kindred Group is a Malta-based online gambling group, operating the Unibet, 32Red, Maria Casino, Bingo.com and Storspelare brands, covering sports betting, casino, poker and bingo for consumers in Europe, Australia and the US. It makes money from betting and gaming margins and employs about 2,000 people. Unibet is a prominent sports-betting name with sponsorship deals in football and other sports. It was listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, and in 2024 it was acquired by France's Francaise des Jeux (FDJ UNITED). Gambling advertising is restricted in many markets, but the brand has strong sport sponsorship experience.

Kota Gold is a boutique jewellery retailer based in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India, whose Crunchbase description says it deals in both traditional and modern jewellery. It is tagged under fashion, jewellery and marketplace, and appears to sell gold and other jewellery to consumers in Tamil Nadu. The scale, number of stores, ownership and the large funding figure shown for it cannot be verified from the available data. It is probably a regional retail brand with limited national consumer visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Side is a US real estate brokerage services company that provides agents and teams with technology, back-office support, marketing, transaction management and a share of commissions, allowing them to run independent practices without building their own brokerage. It also offers a platform to brokerages and agent teams wanting to scale. Based in San Francisco, it supports thousands of agents across many US states. Raised large funding rounds in 2021, including a round of about 250 million dollars. Aimed at real estate professionals, with little direct consumer awareness.

Walnut Coding is an online coding education company for children, with Singapore listed as its base and a presence in several countries, including China and the US. It teaches programming, such as Scratch and Python, through live online classes and curriculums for students typically aged 5 to 18, paid for by parents. The company grew during the pandemic-era online education boom. Reported funding figures are large for a coding-class provider and should be checked. Brand is mostly known to parents in its markets, with limited awareness elsewhere.

Wing Gull EEO appears to be a Beijing-based education technology business in the Haidian district, tagged under EdTech, education and e-learning, and described by Crunchbase as offering an integrated platform, with the rest of the line cut off. AK Altynalmas is a Kazakh gold mining company based in Almaty, owned by the Kazakh state sovereign wealth fund Samruk-Kazyna, developing and operating gold deposits, including the large Kyzyl gold project in East Kazakhstan, and a processing plant. It sells gold doré and concentrate to refiners and the national bank, earning revenue from commodity prices. It has attracted investment for mine construction. B2B and state-owned, with little consumer visibility outside Kazakhstan, though state firms there do sponsor international sport.

Doctor On Demand is a US telehealth provider that connects patients to physicians, psychiatrists, psychologists and other clinicians by video through its mobile app and website, covering urgent care, behavioural health and chronic condition support. It sells mainly through health insurers, employers and health systems, with some direct-to-consumer visits, and earns per-visit and subscription fees. Founded in San Francisco in 2012, it has served millions of members. In 2021 it merged with Grand Rounds to form Included Health. Moderate consumer awareness through employer plans and advertising.

Middle Street Partners is a Charleston, South Carolina, real estate investment firm that describes itself as a multifamily acquisition and development company, with tags covering accounting and construction. It acquires, develops and manages apartment communities, presumably in the Southeastern United States, backed by institutional and private capital. Its portfolio size, the exact markets and the ownership structure are not confirmed in the data. A B2B and investor-oriented firm with essentially no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Pathway Homes is a Dallas, Texas, real estate platform whose Crunchbase description says it has a mission to make housing more accessible, with the line cut off. Its tags list only real estate, and it likely buys, builds or leases single-family homes, but the business model, markets, scale and backers are not confirmed. The September 2022 funding of 225 million dollars points to institutional capital. Probably a small, B2B or investor-backed housing brand with limited public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Purplebricks was a UK online estate agency, founded in 2012 and based in Solihull, that sold or let homes for a fixed upfront fee rather than a percentage commission, using local property experts and an online platform. It expanded to Canada, Australia and the US, closing those businesses between 2019 and 2020 after heavy losses. Listed on the London AIM market, it was a heavy TV advertiser with distinctive purple branding. In 2023 the company was sold to Strike and delisted. Strong consumer awareness in the UK property market, though the business shrank significantly.

RES, Renewable Energy Systems, is a UK-headquartered renewable energy developer, engineering and construction company based in Kings Langley, Hertfordshire, and part of the McAlpine family group. It develops, builds and operates onshore and offshore wind, solar, energy storage and transmission projects, and has delivered over 20 gigawatts of capacity across more than 20 countries. Customers are utilities, corporate energy buyers and governments, and revenue comes from construction contracts, asset management and power sales. Employs well over 2,000 people, with major operations in North America. B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though a prominent name in renewables.

Rockrose Development is a New York City real estate developer, owner and manager of residential rental buildings, with a portfolio of thousands of apartments in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Long Island City, including Chelsea Modern and Lantern House. Founded by Henry Elghanayan in the 1970s, it builds, owns and manages luxury and affordable apartment towers and also operates retail space. Revenue is mainly rent from tenants. It is privately held and family run. Well known in New York property circles, but the brand has little national consumer profile and no sports-marketing record.

SK Bioscience is a South Korean vaccine and biopharmaceutical company, a subsidiary of SK Discovery and part of the SK Group. It develops and manufactures vaccines, including the Skycovione COVID-19 vaccine developed with the University of Washington, makes Novavax vaccines under contract, and has products in typhoid conjugate, chickenpox, flu and pneumococcal vaccines. It acquired the German contract manufacturer IDT Biologika in 2023. Customers include governments, global health bodies such as CEPI and the Gates Foundation, and pharma partners. Listed on the Korea Exchange. B2B and public-health brand with little consumer awareness.

Snagajob is a US online marketplace for hourly and shift-based work, connecting job seekers with employers in restaurants, retail, hospitality, healthcare and logistics. Its website and app let workers search for, apply to and be scheduled for jobs, and employers pay for hiring, job-posting and workforce management tools. It claims over 100 million registered workers. Founded in Virginia in 2000, it is a long-running player in hourly hiring. Privately held with investors. Widely recognised by hourly workers in the US, with some consumer advertising.

Zhongneng United is a Chinese company based in Nanjing, Jiangsu, whose Crunchbase description says it is a B2B enterprise that develops and rents out, with the rest of the line cut off. Its tags include B2B and construction. It appears to be in construction equipment or building-related rental, but the specific products, customers, scale and ownership cannot be confirmed from the available data. It is likely a B2B firm with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Alpha Tau Medical is an Israeli medical technology company developing Alpha DaRT, a cancer treatment in which radium-224-loaded seeds are implanted in solid tumours and release short-range alpha radiation to destroy them, in trials for skin, head and neck, pancreatic, liver and other cancers. It seeks regulatory approvals and partners with hospitals and cancer centres worldwide. Founded in 2015 and based in Jerusalem, it went public on Nasdaq (DRTS) through a SPAC merger in 2022. Revenue is minimal while research continues. B2B and clinical, with little consumer brand profile.

Artis REIT is a Canadian real estate investment trust, based in Winnipeg, that owns commercial property including office, industrial and retail buildings in Canada, mainly the western provinces and Ontario, and in the United States, including Minneapolis, Phoenix and Denver. It earns rental income from business tenants and pays distributions to unit holders. Its portfolio is valued at several billion Canadian dollars. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (AX.UN). B2B landlord brand with no consumer profile and no record of sports sponsorship.

Barkerville Gold Mines was a Canadian gold mining company developing the Cariboo Gold Project and operating the Bonanza Ledge mine in the historic Barkerville area of British Columbia. It was a TSX Venture-listed explorer and developer, taken over by Osisko Gold Royalties in 2019, with its assets later held by Osisko Development. It sold gold and sought financing to build the Cariboo mine. The Crunchbase location entry looks unreliable, since it gives a Northwest Territories town. Resource company with no consumer brand profile.

Bridge Group is a French company based in Paris, described by Crunchbase as a medico-social sector network offering services, with the rest of the line cut off. Its tags cover elder care, family and services. It appears to run or coordinate care and support facilities for older or dependent people, but the facilities, customers, revenue and ownership cannot be confirmed from the data available. Several organisations use similar names. Possibly a care-sector group with local rather than national brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cohabs is a Belgian co-living operator based in Brussels that rents furnished rooms in shared, managed houses, mainly to young professionals and students, with a community and services model. It converts townhouses into shared homes with common living areas, provides utilities, cleaning and events, and charges all-inclusive monthly rents. It has expanded beyond Brussels, backed by real estate investors. Consumer-facing brand among young renters in Belgium, with limited broader awareness. Scale is modest, probably hundreds of rooms.

En+ Group is a Russia-based energy and metals holding company, historically controlled by Oleg Deripaska, with hydropower plants in Siberia, coal and heat generation, and a major stake in aluminium producer Rusal. It lists in London and Moscow and is one of the world's largest low-carbon aluminium and renewable power businesses, with around 19 GW of power capacity. Customers are industrial users and power markets, and revenue comes from aluminium and electricity sales. Sanctions on Deripaska led to a restructuring of its ownership in 2019. B2B conglomerate with little consumer awareness, and sanctions risk makes sponsorship sensitive.

Forbes is a US media and brand company known for Forbes magazine, forbes.com, the Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans, the 30 Under 30 and Global 2000 rankings, events and licensed editions in dozens of countries. Revenue comes from digital advertising, events, memberships, licensing and brand partnerships, with a large contributor network. Founded in 1917, it is based in Jersey City, New Jersey. Hong Kong-based Integrated Whale Media bought a majority stake in 2014, and a SPAC listing planned in 2021 was later terminated. Very strong global business media brand, with an affluent audience of interest to luxury sponsors.

Fountain is a US software company providing a hiring and onboarding platform for hourly and shift workers, used by large employers in logistics, retail, food service and healthcare. The platform automates applicant tracking, interviews, background checks and workflows, so that employers can hire at volume, and customers pay subscription fees. Founded in 2014 and based in San Francisco, it raised a Series C round in 2022. B2B software, with consumer awareness limited to job applicants and little public brand profile.

Hansa Biopharma is a Swedish biopharmaceutical company, based in Lund, developing enzyme therapies that modulate antibodies. Its lead drug imlifidase (Idefirix) is approved in Europe for desensitising highly sensitised kidney transplant patients, and is in late-stage trials for anti-GBM disease and other antibody-driven conditions. It sells through its own commercial team and partners, with revenue still modest. Founded in 2007 and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (HNSA), it has a few hundred employees. Customers are hospitals and transplant centres. B2B pharmaceutical firm with no consumer brand profile.

Pomerleau is a Canadian general contractor and construction manager headquartered in Montreal, building institutional, commercial, industrial, healthcare, transport and energy projects, from hospitals and universities to bridges and condos. Founded in 1885 and still family controlled, it employs several thousand people and operates through offices across Quebec, Ontario, Alberta and British Columbia, with annual revenue in the billions of Canadian dollars. Clients are public bodies, developers and corporations awarding construction contracts. B2B contractor known in Canadian construction circles, with limited consumer profile.

Trilon Group is a US engineering, consulting and infrastructure services business based in Denver, Colorado, tagged under civil engineering and consulting, whose Crunchbase description concerns career paths spanning technical roles. It appears to be a holding of engineering and professional services firms formed with private capital, but its component businesses, customers, scale and owners cannot be confirmed from the available data. It is a B2B group with little consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

YuLife is a London-based insurtech that sells group life insurance, income protection and critical illness cover to employers, bundled with an app that rewards employees with points for healthy activity such as steps and meditation, redeemable for vouchers. Revenue comes from employer premiums. Founded in 2016 by Sammy Rubin, it expanded to the US and South Africa and built a customer base of thousands of employers and hundreds of thousands of insured staff. It raised significant venture funding. Known to employers and employees more than to the general public.

Alameda Health Care is described by Crunchbase as a private healthcare group based in Cairo, Egypt, with the rest of the line cut off. It is tagged under health care and hospitals, and probably operates private hospitals or clinics in Egypt, but its facilities, patient numbers, ownership and scale, including the large funding figure shown, cannot be confirmed from the available data. Probably a regional healthcare brand with limited awareness outside Egypt. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cresud is an Argentine agricultural and real estate company controlled by Eduardo Elsztain, that owns and farms land in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay, producing grain, oilseeds, sugarcane and cattle, and trades farmland. It is the parent of IRSA, one of Argentina's largest commercial property owners with shopping centres and offices in Buenos Aires, and holds a stake in Brasilagro. Revenue comes from crop and livestock sales, land transactions and rent. Based in Buenos Aires, it is listed on Buenos Aires and Nasdaq (CRESY). Corporate brand with little consumer awareness, though IRSA malls are well known in Argentina.

Kaikeba.com is a Chinese online technology education company based in Beijing, offering paid online courses and bootcamps in programming, data analysis, artificial intelligence and product design, aimed at adults building careers in the technology industry and at corporate training. Students pay course fees, and the company partners with employers on hiring. It is a venture-backed startup founded in the late 2010s. Brand awareness is mainly among Chinese tech job seekers, and it has little visibility outside China.

MediWound is an Israeli biopharmaceutical company that develops enzymatic therapies for burns and chronic wounds. Its main product NexoBrid, a bromelain-based enzyme, removes dead burn tissue without surgery, and is approved in Europe, the US and other markets, with US development supported by BARDA, a US government biodefence agency. It is developing EscharEx for chronic ulcers, and sells through partners such as Vericel in North America. Founded in 2000 and based in Yavne, it is listed on Nasdaq (MDWD), and Kamada has been its major shareholder. Customers are hospitals and burn centres. B2B medical company with no consumer profile.

Minerva Project operates Minerva University, a selective four-year undergraduate institution based in San Francisco, founded by entrepreneur Ben Nelson in 2012. Students take small online seminars through the company's own Active Learning Forum platform while rotating through residences in several world cities, including Seoul, Hyderabad, Berlin, Buenos Aires, London and Taipei. Revenue comes from tuition. The company also licensed its technology to other institutions, including a partnership with KGI. It is privately held and backed by venture investors. Strong profile among education innovators and high-achieving international applicants, but small, with a few thousand students.

NextChem is the technology and green chemistry arm of the Italian engineering group MAIRE (formerly Maire Tecnimont), based in Rome. It licenses process technologies and provides engineering for fertilisers, polymers, circular plastics, hydrogen, biofuels and carbon capture, and its subsidiary MyRechemical works on chemical recycling of plastics. Customers are industrial, chemical and energy companies, and income comes from licences, engineering and equipment contracts. The parent trades on Borsa Italiana, which probably explains why this row is flagged as listed. The input location shows Venezuela, which looks like a data error. B2B with little consumer awareness.

Pluri, formerly Pluristem Therapeutics, is an Israeli biotechnology company based in Haifa that develops placenta-derived cell therapy products, known as PLX cells, using a 3D cell-culture technology. It targets conditions such as muscle injury, acute radiation syndrome and critical limb ischemia, and has expanded its platform into food-tech, cultivated meat and agriculture, under the Pluri name adopted in 2022. Revenue is small and comes from collaboration and services, while research is funded by equity. Listed on Nasdaq (PLUR) and the Tel Aviv exchange. B2B and clinical, with no consumer brand recognition.

Aiper is a consumer robotics brand best known for cordless robotic pool cleaners, including the Scuba, Seagull and Surfer lines, plus pool skimmers and related devices. It sells to homeowners through Amazon, its own website and retailers in the US, Europe and Asia, and competes with Maytronics' Dolphin and Zodiac. The company was founded in Shenzhen in 2018 and has a US office in the Atlanta area. Growing consumer brand in the pool and outdoor segments with a strong online and e-commerce presence, and a record of heavy digital advertising.

Aprea Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, originally a Swedish spin-out from the Karolinska Institute and now based in the US, developing cancer drugs for DNA damage response, including ATR inhibitor ATRN-119 and WEE1 inhibitor APR-1051. It previously worked on eprenetapopt, which failed a late-stage trial in myelodysplastic syndrome. It is listed on Nasdaq (APRE), has no commercial products, and finances itself through equity raises and grants. Customers would eventually be oncology providers. B2B development-stage biotech with no consumer profile and a limited budget.

April Bio is a South Korean biotechnology company in Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, and Crunchbase calls it a drug development company, with tags for biopharma and biotechnology. The funding figure of 244.8 billion appears to be in Korean won, so it is roughly a few hundred million US dollars at most, and the June 2026 date points to a recent raise or listing event. Its pipeline, products, partners and listing venue cannot be confirmed from the data. Pre-commercial drug developers have no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

End2End Holdings is a Danish company based in Aalborg that Crunchbase describes as a provider of outsourced solutions for mobile operators, tagged under mobile and telecommunications. The dated funding entry from 2003 suggests an old venture round, so the entity may now be dormant or renamed. B2B telecom services supplier with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Fusion Connect was a US provider of cloud communications and connectivity, selling hosted voice (UCaaS), SD-WAN, internet access, security and managed network services to small and mid-sized businesses and enterprise customers, mainly in North America. It was created through the 2018 merger of Fusion Telecommunications and Birch Communications, and collected recurring monthly fees. Heavy debt led to a Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2019, and it emerged under lender control with new management. B2B telecom brand with little consumer awareness.

Hangshun Chip is a Chinese electronics company in Shenzhen, Guangdong, whose Crunchbase description says it is an electronics research and manufacturing business, tagged under AI infrastructure and applications. It likely designs or makes chips or electronic components for AI-related applications, but the specific products, customers, scale and ownership are not confirmed from the available data. The yuan 1.1 billion funding figure and June 2022 date point to a significant raise. B2B hardware supplier with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Karat is a US company that provides technical interviewing as a service: its trained engineers, called Interview Engineers, run structured coding and system-design interviews on behalf of employers, returning scored evidence to recruiters and hiring managers, and it offers an interview platform and a talent marketplace. Customers include large technology companies, banks and consumer firms. Revenue comes from per-interview fees and subscriptions. Founded in 2014 and based in Seattle, it has conducted hundreds of thousands of interviews. B2B product, known in engineering hiring circles but not to the general public.

Lument is a US commercial real estate finance firm, formerly Hunt Real Estate Capital, that provides multifamily, seniors housing and healthcare lending through agency programmes such as Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA, plus balance-sheet loans and bridge financing. It is owned by ORIX, the Japanese financial group, and has an affiliated listed vehicle, Lument Finance Trust (NYSE: LFT). Based in New York, it originates and services loans for borrowers across the US, with billions of dollars in annual loan volume. B2B lender with little consumer awareness.

MeMed is an Israeli diagnostics company that has developed host-immune response tests to tell bacterial from viral infections. Its MeMed BV test, run on the MeMed Key analyser, measures the blood levels of three proteins (TRAIL, IP-10 and CRP) and returns a score within minutes, helping doctors decide when antibiotics are needed. It is sold to hospitals and urgent care centres in Europe, the US and other markets, with FDA clearance and CE marking, and has a sepsis-related pipeline. Founded in 2009 and based in Haifa, it is venture backed. B2B medical device company with no consumer profile.

RenoRun is a Montreal-based construction technology startup building an online platform for general contractors, renovators and building-material suppliers, with the aim of simplifying ordering, delivery and procurement of materials for projects. Revenue comes from material sales and platform fees from professional contractors. It was founded in the late 2010s and is venture backed. Its pitch is a single-source platform for contractors, competing with big-box retailers and building-supply distributors. B2B firm with brand awareness mostly limited to the Canadian trade.

Shikun & Binui is Israel's largest construction and infrastructure group, based in Airport City near Ben Gurion airport. It builds housing, roads, rail, water and energy infrastructure in Israel and abroad, develops real estate, and owns concession and renewable energy assets through its Shikun & Binui Energy and Water divisions, with operations in Africa, Latin America and Europe. Customers are government bodies, municipalities and homebuyers. Controlled by the Arison family's holding company, it is listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and has several thousand employees. Well-known Israeli construction name, with little recognition internationally.

Xinyi Glass Holdings is one of China's largest glass makers, producing float glass, architectural glass, and automobile glass, selling to construction firms and to vehicle makers and the replacement-glass market. Founded in 1988 and controlled by the Tung family, it is listed on the Hong Kong exchange (0868) and has revenue in the tens of billions of Hong Kong dollars. B2B, with little consumer recognition although car owners may meet its brand on windscreens.

Tecton is a US machine learning infrastructure company, founded in 2019 by the team that built Uber's Michelangelo platform, that sells a feature store and feature platform for building, serving and managing the data inputs to real-time AI models. B2B developer software with no consumer brand.

Eco Baltia is a Latvian environmental services group, with Riga headquarters, that collects and recycles waste and packaging in the Baltic states. Its businesses include Clean R, the largest Latvian waste management company, and Eco Baltia vide, covering waste collection, packaging-deposit handling, and recycling and processing of plastic, paper and metals. Customers are municipalities, businesses and households, and revenue comes from collection fees, recycled material sales and packaging schemes. A B2B and municipal services brand with some local consumer recognition in Latvia.

Nexii is a building technology company that developed a prefabricated wall and building system using a proprietary magnesium-based material called Nexiite, intended to give low-carbon, fast construction for homes, warehouses and commercial buildings. Founded in Vancouver, Canada, it built manufacturing plants for its wall panels in North America and went public through a SPAC merger. It faced financial problems and entered insolvency proceedings in 2023. B2B construction supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Properly is a Canadian tech-enabled real estate brokerage, founded in 2017 in Toronto, that helps homeowners sell or buy with a flat-fee service backed by technology, a home valuation tool and in-house agents. It focuses on the Greater Toronto Area and has expanded to other parts of Ontario and further afield. Revenue comes from commissions and from add-on services such as renovation and bridging finance. It is venture backed. Moderate consumer awareness in Toronto through online and outdoor advertising.

Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy is an Indian solar engineering, procurement and construction contractor, with a heritage in the Shapoorji Pallonji group's electro-mechanical engineering business. It builds utility-scale solar plants across India, the Middle East, Africa, Australia, the US and Europe, and offers operations and maintenance, having installed many gigawatts of solar capacity. It was listed on the NSE and BSE in 2019, and in 2022 Reliance New Energy bought a roughly 40 percent stake, becoming its largest shareholder. Customers are power developers, utilities and government-backed projects. B2B contractor with limited consumer awareness.

Uzmetkombinat is Uzbekistan's leading steelmaker, based at Bekobod in Tashkent region, producing long steel products such as rebar, wire rod and sections from scrap, and selling mainly to construction firms and industry in Uzbekistan and neighbouring Central Asian markets. It is a state-linked enterprise with a history stretching back to the Soviet period. Revenue comes from steel product sales. B2B heavy industry brand with little consumer awareness outside the region.

Epiroc is a Swedish mining and infrastructure equipment company, spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018, that makes rock drilling rigs, underground loaders and trucks, mining and construction tools, and also software, automation and aftermarket services. Customers are mining companies and construction contractors worldwide, with a large share of revenue from service and parts. Headquartered in Nacka near Stockholm, it has roughly 18,000 employees and revenue of about 60 billion Swedish kronor. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (EPI A and EPI B). B2B industrial brand, well known in mining, but not to consumers.

Equillium is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing itolizumab, an anti-CD6 antibody, for immune and inflammatory conditions including acute graft-versus-host disease, lupus nephritis and other autoimmune disorders. It has a licence deal with Ono Pharmaceutical in Japan and with Biocon for itolizumab, and receives revenue from partners rather than from products. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (EQ), it has a small team. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand and limited marketing funds.

Aptevo Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company that develops bispecific cancer immunotherapies, including mipletamig (APVO436) for acute myeloid leukemia and ALG.APV-527 for solid tumours, using its ADAPTIR and ADAPTIR-FLEX platforms. It was spun off from Emergent BioSolutions in 2016, sold its marketed hemophilia products, and is now a development-stage firm without product revenue. Based in Seattle and listed on Nasdaq (APVO). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Arco Educacao, also known as Arco Platform, is a Brazilian education company that sells complete learning systems to private K-12 schools, including textbooks, digital platforms, teacher training and assessments, under brands such as Anglo, PAR, NAME, Nave a Vela and Eleva. Schools subscribe annually to the content and pedagogy, and the company serves hundreds of thousands of students in Brazil. Founded in 2004 and listed on Nasdaq (ARCE) in 2018. Customers are private schools, with parents as the end users. B2B brand, known to Brazilian school owners rather than the public.

Baladna is a Qatari dairy and food company, founded in 2017 by Moutaz Al Khayyat during the Gulf blockade of Qatar to make the country self-sufficient in fresh milk, and operating a large farm near Doha with tens of thousands of cows. It produces fresh milk, laban, yoghurt, cheese and juices, sold across Qatar and exported to other Gulf and regional markets, and has expanded production to Egypt and Algeria. Listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange since 2021. Strong consumer brand in Qatar, a supermarket staple with substantial local marketing.

Bliss GVS Pharma is an Indian pharmaceutical manufacturer in Mumbai that makes and exports generic formulations, including antimalarials, anti-infectives, pain relievers and women's health products, and sells condoms and contraceptive products in tenders. Customers are government agencies, global health programmes and distributors, with exports to Africa, Latin America and other emerging markets, and a domestic business. It is listed on the BSE and NSE and has manufacturing plants in Palghar and elsewhere. Consumer brand awareness is moderate in India for its condom and OTC lines, but sponsorship capacity is limited.

Boingo Wireless is a US wireless infrastructure company that designs, builds and operates Wi-Fi and distributed antenna system networks in airports, stadiums, military bases and campuses, and sells Wi-Fi and cellular connectivity to carriers, venue owners and consumers. It operates networks for US military housing, airports like Dallas Fort Worth, and large events, and it also sold Wi-Fi subscriptions under the Boingo brand. DigitalBridge acquired Boingo in 2021 for about 850 million dollars, taking it private. It was founded in 2001 and run from Los Angeles. Moderate consumer awareness among air travellers.

FibroBiologics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing fibroblast cell therapies, using patient-derived or donor fibroblasts, for conditions such as degenerative disc disease, multiple sclerosis, diabetic foot ulcers and psoriasis. It is based in Houston, and listed on Nasdaq (FBLG) after a 2024 IPO. It has no approved products and finances itself through equity. Customers would eventually be physicians and hospitals. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and little marketing budget.

Gia Lai Electricity is a Vietnamese power company, with its head office in Ho Chi Minh City, that owns hydropower plants in the Central Highlands province of Gia Lai and has added wind and solar farms. It sells electricity into the national grid under power purchase agreements with the state-owned utility EVN, so its revenue depends on water levels, wind and tariff rules. It is listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (GEG). B2B utility with little consumer awareness outside the investment community.

Hepion Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing rencofilstat, a cyclophilin inhibitor, for liver diseases including NASH, now called MASH, hepatocellular carcinoma and other fibrosis indications. It has no marketed product and relies on equity funding. Based in Morristown, New Jersey, and previously known as ContraVir Pharmaceuticals, it is listed on Nasdaq (HEPA), though its financial position has been weak. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and negligible sponsorship budget.

iMDx is a Nashville, Tennessee, company tagged by Crunchbase under biotechnology, health care and related areas, and flagged here as listed. The entry has no description, and several unrelated companies use the iMDx name, so it cannot be tied to a specific business, product or parent from the available data. Its products, customers, scale and listing venue need to be confirmed. Early-stage health companies of this kind have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

INmune Bio is a US clinical-stage immunology company developing drugs that target innate immune dysfunction and inflammation, led by XPro1595, a TNF inhibitor in trials for Alzheimer's disease, and INKmune, a cell-based therapy for cancer. It has no marketed products and finances operations through equity raises. Headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida, with research links to UK and Australian groups, it is listed on Nasdaq (INMB). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile, and small marketing resources.

Itafos is a phosphate fertiliser and specialty products company with operations in North America, mainly the Conda phosphate mine and plant complex in Idaho, plus the Arraias project in Brazil and the Farim development in Senegal. It sells monoammonium phosphate (MAP), superphosphoric acid and merchant-grade phosphoric acid to farmers and distributors in North America, and exports to other markets. It is headquartered in Houston and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (IFOS). B2B commodity producer with little consumer awareness.

Marker Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing multi-antigen-targeted T cell therapies (MultiTAA) for blood cancers and solid tumours, using non-engineered T cells grown from patients' own blood. Its lead programme treats lymphoma and acute myeloid leukemia, with grant support from the Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas, and research ties to Baylor College of Medicine. Based in Houston, it is listed on Nasdaq (MRKR) and has no commercial products. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand.

MetaVia, formerly NeuroBo Pharmaceuticals, is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company working on drugs for obesity and cardiometabolic disease, led by DA-1726 (a dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist) and DA-1241 for liver disease, licensed from Korea's Dong-A ST. Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (MTVA), it has no commercial products and depends on equity financing. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile and limited funds for marketing.

Newron Pharmaceuticals is an Italian biopharmaceutical company, based in Bresso near Milan, developing treatments for central nervous system diseases. Its lead candidate evenamide is in late-stage trials as an add-on for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, and it receives royalties on Xadago (safinamide) for Parkinson's disease, which is sold by Zambon and partners worldwide. It also has other neurology programmes. Founded in 1998 and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (NWRN), it has a small team of tens of employees. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Nuvectis Pharma is a US clinical-stage oncology company developing targeted drugs for cancers with high unmet need, including NXP800 for ARID1A-mutated cancers such as ovarian clear-cell carcinoma and NXP900, an inhibitor of the SRC kinase family. NXP800 has received FDA fast track and orphan designations. Based in Fort Lee, New Jersey, it was founded in 2020 and listed on Nasdaq (NVCT) in 2022. It has no revenue and is funded through equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand.

Phio Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing self-delivering RNA interference therapeutics, under the INTASYL name, that silence genes to boost immune cells' ability to fight cancer, with a lead programme PH-762 for skin cancers. It was formerly RXi Pharmaceuticals and has deep roots in RNAi research at the University of Massachusetts. Based in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, with no marketed products, it is listed on Nasdaq (PHIO). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and a small budget.

Shinsegae Engineering and Construction is a South Korean builder, based in Seoul and part of the Shinsegae retail group, that constructs apartments, offices, retail complexes, hotels and civil engineering projects, including department stores and shopping centres for its group affiliates. Customers include the parent group, developers and public bodies, and revenue comes from construction contracts, which gives it a captive pipeline. It is listed on the Korea Exchange. B2B contractor with limited consumer awareness, although the parent Shinsegae group is a household retail name in Korea.

Slate Office REIT is a Canadian real estate investment trust, managed by Slate Asset Management in Toronto, that owns office buildings in Canada, mainly in Ontario, Quebec and Alberta, leased to government and corporate tenants. It earns rental income and pays distributions to unit holders. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (SOT.UN) and has faced debt and occupancy pressure since the pandemic. B2B landlord with no consumer brand profile.

Youran Dairy is a Chinese dairy farming company based in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, that raises dairy cattle and produces raw milk sold to dairy processors, and also produces forage and feed. It operates large farms with tens of thousands of cows in northern China, and its revenue depends on raw milk prices and herd productivity. It is listed on the Hong Kong exchange. B2B agricultural producer with no consumer brand, and a limited marketing profile.

AEON Biopharma is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing ABP-450, a botulinum toxin complex, for therapeutic uses such as chronic migraine and cervical dystonia, with aesthetic rights licensed to Evolus. Based in Irvine, California, it was listed on the NYSE American (AEON) in 2023 via a SPAC merger with Priveterra. It has no commercial revenue and depends on equity financing. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Annovis Bio is a US clinical-stage drug developer working on buntanetap, an oral drug aimed at neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, by lowering the production of several neurotoxic proteins. It has run Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials, has no commercial products, and relies on equity raises and grants. Founded by Maria Maccecchini, a longtime biotech executive, and based in Malvern, Pennsylvania, it is listed on the NYSE (ANVS). B2B drug developer with no consumer brand.

Beam Global makes and sells solar-powered electric vehicle charging systems, notably the EV ARC, a self-contained, off-grid, rapidly deployable charger that needs no trenching or grid connection, plus solar-powered street lighting and battery storage products. Customers include municipalities, universities, fleets and the US military, with sales mainly in North America and Europe following its acquisition of the Italian firm Amiga. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (BEEM), it reports annual revenue of tens of millions of dollars. B2B brand with some profile among fleet and municipal buyers.

Betterlife Pharma is a Canadian biotechnology company based in Vancouver that develops psychedelic-derived drug candidates, including LSD and MDMA-related compounds, for anxiety, depression and related mental health conditions. It is listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and has a small team and limited revenue. Funding comes from private placements and warrants. B2B and development stage, with little consumer awareness and constrained marketing funds.

Biodexa Pharmaceuticals is a UK clinical-stage specialty pharmaceutical company based in Cardiff, Wales, developing treatments for rare and serious diseases, led by eRapa (encapsulated rapamycin) for familial adenomatous polyposis, plus tolimidone for type 1 diabetes and a brain tumour candidate. It uses a proprietary drug-delivery technology platform. It is listed on Nasdaq (BDRX) and funds itself through equity raises. Formerly Midatech Pharma, it was renamed in 2023. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Biotalys is a Belgian agricultural biotechnology company, based in Ghent, that develops protein-based biocontrol products for crop protection, led by Evoca for fruit and vegetable disease control, targeting fungal diseases and insects. It was spun out of Flanders research institute VIB and sells to growers via distribution partners, with a US EPA registration for Evoca obtained in 2023. Listed on Euronext Brussels (BTLS). Customers are farmers and agri-input distributors. B2B agri-tech firm with no consumer brand.

Brazil Potash is a development-stage mining company holding the Autazes potash project in the Amazonas state of Brazil, which it aims to build as a large domestic source of potassium chloride fertiliser. Brazil imports the vast majority of the potash that its farmers use, so the project targets that import-dependent agricultural market, with customers expected to be fertiliser blenders and agribusiness groups. The company is run from Toronto with a Brazilian subsidiary and is listed on the NYSE American (GRO) following a 2024 IPO. It has no mine revenue yet and faces permitting and financing steps. B2B resources developer with no consumer profile.

BriaCell Therapeutics is a clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing Bria-IMT, a whole-cell cancer vaccine based on engineered breast cancer cell lines, used with checkpoint inhibitors in late-stage metastatic breast cancer, alongside other cell-therapy candidates. It operates between Philadelphia and Vancouver, and is listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (BCTX). It has no approved product and depends on equity raises. Customers would eventually be oncology clinics and hospitals. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Calidi Biotherapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing cell-based delivery of oncolytic viruses, in which stem cells carry cancer-killing viruses to tumours, with candidates such as CLD-101 and CLD-201 in early trials. It is based in San Diego and listed on the NYSE American (CLDI) following a 2023 SPAC merger with First Light Acquisition Group. It has no products on the market and relies on equity financing. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and a small marketing budget.

Cannara Biotech is a Canadian cannabis producer based in Montreal, operating a large greenhouse and processing site in Valleyfield, Quebec, and growing cannabis for the adult-use market under several consumer brands, sold through provincial wholesalers and retail stores, mainly in Quebec and other provinces. It positions itself as a low-cost producer, with revenue in the tens of millions of Canadian dollars. Founded by Quebec entrepreneurs, it is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (LOVE). Canadian cannabis advertising rules heavily limit sponsorship use.

Cardiff Oncology is a US clinical-stage oncology company developing onvansertib, an oral PLK1 inhibitor, mainly for RAS-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with standard chemotherapy and bevacizumab, with additional studies in other tumours. It has no commercial product and funds research through equity raises and grants. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (CRDF), it has a team of a few dozen employees. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Cardiol Therapeutics is a Canadian clinical-stage life science company, based in Oakville, Ontario, developing cannabidiol-based and other cardiovascular drugs. Its lead product CardiolRx, a pharmaceutical-grade oral cannabidiol, is in trials for recurrent pericarditis and acute myocarditis, with a subcutaneous candidate for heart failure also in development. It is listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (CRDL), has no approved products, and raises money through equity offerings. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

CEL-SCI is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Vienna, Virginia, developing Multikine (leukocyte interleukin injection), an immunotherapy given before surgery and radiation in newly diagnosed advanced head and neck cancer, which has completed a large Phase 3 trial. It also owns manufacturing facilities near Baltimore. It has no approved product and funds itself through equity issues. Listed on NYSE American (CVM). Long-running but small B2B biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Central Pattana is Thailand's largest retail property developer, owning and operating shopping centres such as CentralWorld, Central Plaza Lat Phrao, Central Festival, Central Westgate and Central Village, plus office buildings, hotels, residential projects and mixed-use developments, in Bangkok and provincial cities. Revenue comes from rent, service fees and property sales. It is part of the Central Group of the Chirathivat family and is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (CPN) with a very large market capitalisation. Its malls attract tens of millions of Thai and tourist visitors, so it is a well-known consumer-facing property brand in Thailand.

Cocrystal Pharma is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antiviral drugs for influenza, coronaviruses including COVID-19, and norovirus, using structure-based drug design. Lead candidates are an oral influenza A/B treatment and protease inhibitors for coronaviruses. It partners with outside groups for trials and has no product revenue. Based in Bothell, Washington, with research roots in Miami, it is listed on Nasdaq (COCP). B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Coloured Ties Capital is a Calgary, Alberta, company that Crunchbase tags under agriculture and energy efficiency, flagged here as listed. No business description is given in the data. It appears to be a small investment or holding company linked to those sectors, but its portfolio, products, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the available information. Very small listed companies of this kind have limited public profiles and no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cosciens Biopharma, formerly Aeterna Zentaris, is a Toronto-based specialty biopharmaceutical company. Its commercial product Macrilen (macimorelin) is an oral diagnostic test for adult growth hormone deficiency, licensed to partners for different regions, and it has other pipeline candidates in oncology and endocrinology. Revenue is modest and comes from licensing and milestone payments. The shares are listed on Nasdaq and the TSX. B2B pharma business with no consumer profile.

CytoDyn is a US biotechnology company, based in Vancouver, Washington, developing leronlimab, a humanised monoclonal antibody that blocks the CCR5 receptor, studied for HIV, cancer, NASH and COVID-19. Its COVID-19 programme drew intense attention in 2020 and 2021, but regulators did not authorise it, and the company later faced legal disputes and a major reorganisation of its board. It has no approved product and trades on the OTC markets (CYDY). B2B drug developer with no consumer brand, and a troubled history that makes it a poor sponsorship prospect.

Dare Bioscience is a US women's health biopharmaceutical company that develops and commercialises products for contraception, menopause, vaginal health and sexual health. Its approved product Xaciato (clindamycin vaginal gel) for bacterial vaginosis is licensed to Organon, and its pipeline includes Ovaprene, a hormone-free monthly vaginal contraceptive, and Sildenafil Cream for female sexual arousal disorder. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (DARE), it earns licence revenue and milestones. Customers are gynaecologists and patients through partners. Little consumer brand awareness.

Decibel Cannabis Company is a Calgary-based Canadian cannabis producer and brand house, selling flower, vapes and edibles under consumer brands such as Qwest and Blendcraft through provincial wholesalers and its own Alberta retail presence. It earns revenue from wholesale supply of packaged consumer goods and is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Canadian cannabis marketing restrictions limit brand-building, and sponsorship use is heavily restricted. Moderate awareness among Canadian cannabis consumers, small by industry standards.

Edesa Biotech is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Markham, Ontario, focused on immuno-inflammatory and immuno-oncology treatments. Its lead products are EB05, an antibody for acute respiratory distress syndrome that was tested in COVID-19, and EB01, a topical for chronic allergic contact dermatitis, plus an anti-TLR4 cancer programme. It has no approved products and finances itself through equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (EDSA). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Fengyuan Pharmaceutical is a Chinese pharmaceutical and biotechnology business based in Hefei, Anhui, tagged under biotechnology and health care and flagged as listed. Beyond that, the Crunchbase entry gives no description, so the products, such as traditional Chinese medicines or generics, the customers, scale and ownership are not confirmed from the available data. Chinese pharmaceutical manufacturers typically sell through hospitals and distributors and have limited consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

FIH Mobile is a Hong Kong-listed subsidiary of Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry) that manufactures mobile phones and other electronic devices on a contract basis, including design and engineering services, for global handset brands. It has factories in China, India and Vietnam, and has worked for customers such as HMD (Nokia-branded phones) and several Asian smartphone makers. Revenue is in the billions of dollars and it employs tens of thousands of people. Pure B2B contract manufacturer with no consumer brand of its own, and closely tied to Foxconn.

Genelux is a US late-stage clinical biotechnology company developing oncolytic viral immunotherapies, led by Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec), a modified vaccinia virus in a Phase 3 trial for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, with additional work in lung and pancreatic cancer. Based in Westlake Village, California, and founded by Dr Aladar Szalay, it listed on Nasdaq (GNLX) in 2023. It has no commercial products and funds research through equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand.

Geregu Power is a Nigerian gas-fired power generation company, owning the Geregu power plant in Kogi State, with installed capacity of several hundred megawatts across its original and newer units. It sells electricity into the national grid, and its customers are the Nigerian bulk electricity trader and distribution companies. It is part of the Mainstream Energy Solutions group, which bought the plant in the Nigerian power privatisation of the early 2010s. Head office is in Lagos. B2B power producer with limited consumer awareness.

Grace Therapeutics, formerly Acasti Pharma, is a specialty pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq, developing GTX-104, an intravenous formulation of nimodipine for aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage, which is aimed at hospital intensive care units and intended to replace oral dosing. It also holds earlier assets from its past as a cardiovascular company. Based in Laval, Quebec. No commercial revenue yet, and funded through equity and licensing deals. B2B pharma business with no consumer brand.

Grid AI is a Boca Raton, Florida, company that Crunchbase tags under biotechnology and health care, flagged as listed. The record has no description, and the name suggests an AI-related business, so the tags and name do not obviously match. The company cannot be identified with confidence, and the product, customers, ownership and listing venue need to be checked. Small listed health technology firms have little consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

HCW Biologics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing immunotherapies based on its TOBI discovery platform, which creates fusion proteins that activate natural killer cells and T cells, aimed at cancers and age-related inflammatory disease. Lead candidates include HCW9302 for alopecia areata and other autoimmune conditions. It is listed on Nasdaq (HCWB) and has no commercial products. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and a small marketing budget.

HemoGenyx Pharmaceuticals is a small US biotechnology company, based in New York, developing a stem cell therapy approach for blood disorders and certain autoimmune diseases, aimed at replacing bone marrow transplants with a safer conditioning treatment. Its programmes remained preclinical or at an early clinical stage. It trades on the over-the-counter markets and has very limited resources. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

iBio is a US biotechnology company that has evolved from a plant-based contract development and manufacturing business into an AI-driven drug discovery and biologics developer, with programmes in obesity and cardiometabolic disease, oncology and antibody engineering. It sold its Texas CDMO facility and now concentrates on its discovery platform and pipeline, partly in cooperation with partners. Based in Newark, Delaware, with offices in San Diego, it is listed on NYSE American (IBIO). B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

J-Pharma is a Japanese biotechnology and pharmaceutical company based in Tokyo, tagged by Crunchbase under biotechnology and medical, and flagged here as listed. No description is available in the input. It appears to be a drug developer or specialty pharma business, but its products, pipeline, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed. Japanese specialty pharma firms usually sell through hospitals and wholesalers and have no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Kiora Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage ophthalmology company developing small-molecule drugs for retinal diseases, led by KIO-301, a photoswitch molecule intended to restore light sensitivity in blind retinal cells for retinitis pigmentosa, which is licensed in Asia to Senju Pharmaceutical. It has other earlier candidates for inflammatory eye conditions. Based in Encinitas, California, and listed on Nasdaq (KPRX), it has no approved product and relies on equity financing and partner payments. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Lucid Diagnostics is a US commercial-stage medical diagnostics company, a majority-owned subsidiary of PAVmed, selling the EsoCheck cell collection device and EsoGuard DNA test to screen for Barrett's esophagus and detect risk of esophageal cancer in people with chronic acid reflux. It sells through its own centres and to physicians, with payers gradually reimbursing the test. Based in New York and listed on Nasdaq (LUCD), it has small revenue and heavy losses. Consumer awareness is low, though it markets to patients with reflux.

MindMaze, formerly Relief Therapeutics, is a Geneva-based Swiss pharmaceutical group listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange. Relief developed and marketed specialty and rare disease products and pursued the inhaled aviptadil drug for lung disease. The change of name points to a combination with MindMaze, a neurotechnology business known for digital therapeutics for stroke and brain injury rehabilitation, also Swiss-based. Details of the combined business should be checked. B2B healthcare company with no consumer profile.

Mirvac Group is one of Australia's largest diversified property groups, listed on the ASX (MGR) and based in Sydney. It develops and owns office towers, retail centres, industrial and logistics property and build-to-rent apartments, and builds residential communities and apartment projects for sale, with a development pipeline worth many billions of Australian dollars. Revenue comes from rent, apartment and land sales, and funds management. Mirvac is a recognised consumer-facing property brand in Sydney and Melbourne for homebuyers, and has used sports and event sponsorship.

Moleculin Biotech is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing oncology drugs for hard-to-treat cancers, led by Annamycin, an anthracycline designed to avoid cardiotoxicity and drug resistance, in trials for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia and soft tissue sarcoma lung metastases. It also has WP1066 for brain tumours and WP1122 for viral infections. Based in Houston and listed on Nasdaq (MBRX), it has no approved product and depends on equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

NeOnc Technologies is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing brain cancer therapies built around perillyl alcohol derivatives, led by NEO100 and NEO212, which are designed to cross the blood-brain barrier, targeting glioblastoma and other high-grade gliomas. Based in Calabasas, California, with strong ties to the University of Southern California research tradition, it listed on Nasdaq (NTHI) in 2025. It has no commercial products. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

NervGen Pharma is a Canadian clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Vancouver, developing NVG-291, a peptide designed to enable repair of damaged nerve connections after spinal cord injury, tested in the CONNECT SCI trial in chronic and acute injury. It also looks at other neurological conditions. It has no approved product, is funded by equity and partner contributions, and is listed on the TSX (NGEN) and OTC markets. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Nuwellis is a US medical device company that makes the Aquadex SmartFlow system, an ultrafiltration therapy that removes excess fluid from patients with fluid overload, such as those with heart failure, and the Vivian blood-purification system for kidney-related care. It sells to hospitals and critical care units, and has a pediatric version. Formerly CHF Solutions, it is based in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, and listed on Nasdaq (NUWE) with small revenue. B2B medical device company with no consumer brand profile.

Opus Genetics, formerly Ocuphire Pharma, is a US clinical-stage ophthalmology company developing gene therapies for inherited retinal diseases such as LCA5 and BEST1-related conditions, alongside phentolamine eye drops for reversal of mydriasis, presbyopia and dim-light vision disturbances. It licensed phentolamine to Viatris. Based in Farmington Hills, Michigan, with research operations in the Durham area, it is listed on Nasdaq (IRD). Revenue comes from licensing and grants. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Pelthos Therapeutics is a US commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company, formed in 2025 through a merger involving Channel Therapeutics and Ligand's LNHC unit. It markets Zelsuvmi (berdazimer gel), a topical treatment for molluscum contagiosum approved by the FDA, in the paediatric dermatology market. Based in North Brunswick, New Jersey, and listed on NYSE American (PTHS), it sells through specialty pharmacies and dermatology practices. Customers are dermatologists and parents. B2B pharma with little consumer brand awareness.

Profusa is a US biosensor company developing tissue-integrated sensors, notably the Lumee oxygen-sensing platform, a tiny injectable hydrogel sensor that reads oxygen levels through the skin, intended for monitoring peripheral artery disease and critical limb ischemia and for wider health tracking. Founded in 2009 and based in Emeryville, California, it listed on Nasdaq (PFSA) via a 2024 SPAC merger. Revenue is minimal, mainly from grants and early commercial work. B2B medical technology with no consumer brand profile.

Quantum Biopharma, formerly FSD Pharma, is a Canadian biotechnology company based in Toronto, with a lead programme Lucid-MS for multiple sclerosis, a neuroprotective compound aimed at stopping myelin damage, plus Celly Nutrition, a consumer sports nutrition and wellness brand, and legacy interests in cannabis cultivation. It trades on Nasdaq and the Canadian Securities Exchange (QNTM). Revenue is small. Mostly pharma development, with a small consumer arm, Celly, with limited awareness.

Tempest Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage oncology company developing small-molecule drugs for cancers, led by amezalpat (TPST-1120), a PPAR-alpha antagonist being trialled with atezolizumab and bevacizumab in first-line hepatocellular carcinoma, and TPST-1495 targeting the EP2/EP4 pathway. It has no commercial products and funds research by equity raises. Based in Brisbane, California, and listed on Nasdaq (TPST). B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

TenNor Therapeutics is a clinical-stage anti-infective company, founded in China with operations in the US, developing new antibiotics for drug-resistant bacterial infections, including rifasutenizol (TNP-2092) for Helicobacter pylori and a series of candidates against resistant staph infections. It combines research in Suzhou with a US presence in New Jersey. It has raised venture funding and has no approved products. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Traws Pharma is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, formed in 2024 by the merger of Onconova Therapeutics with Trawsfynydd Therapeutics, developing oral antivirals against influenza, including bird flu, and COVID-19, along with oncology drug rigosertib. Based in Newtown, Pennsylvania, it is listed on Nasdaq (TRAW). It has no product revenue and is funded by equity raises. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Valerio Therapeutics, formerly Onxeo, is a French biotechnology company based in the Paris area (Villejuif) that develops DNA damage response cancer drugs, including its AsiDNA platform of decoy molecules that interfere with tumour DNA repair. Listed on Euronext Paris, it has no commercial products and depends on equity financing and partnerships. Customers would be oncology providers. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and a very small team.

Vitru Education is a Brazilian higher education company, listed on Nasdaq (VTRU), that operates the Unicesumar and UniFTC brands. It provides undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, mostly distance learning, through a network of study centres across Brazil, with hundreds of thousands of students. Revenue comes from tuition fees. It was formed through the combination of Unicesumar's owner with a Brazilian education group, then expanded by acquisition. Based in Sao Paulo, it is a large private distance-learning operator. Education brand known in Brazil through local advertising, with limited global recognition.

Vivakor is a US company listed on Nasdaq (VIVK), based in Dallas, that has pivoted from remediation technology to oil gathering, storage, transportation and processing. It runs crude oil logistics and storage in Texas and other states, and uses soil remediation technology to recover oil from contaminated soils. Customers are refiners, oil producers and industrial users. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars, and it acquired Silver Fuels Delhi. B2B energy services firm with no consumer profile.

VivoSim Labs, formerly Organovo Holdings, is a US biotechnology company that develops 3D bioprinted and lab-grown human tissue models used to test drug toxicity and efficacy for pharmaceutical customers, as an alternative to animal testing. After a pivot from therapeutic tissue development it sold its FXR program to Lilly and rebranded in 2025. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (VIVS). B2B research-tools supplier with no consumer profile.

VolitionRx is a US-and-Belgium diagnostics company developing Nu.Q, a blood-based epigenetics platform that detects circulating nucleosomes for cancer screening and monitoring, including lung and colorectal tests and a veterinary cancer test for dogs. It sells research and lab-developed products and aims at regulatory approval for clinical use. Run from Henderson, Nevada, with laboratories in Namur, Belgium, and listed on NYSE American (VNRX). Revenue is tiny. B2B diagnostics firm with no consumer brand.

Small B2B life sciences platform with no consumer brand profile.

Japan Communications Inc. (JCI) is a Japanese mobile telecom company, based in Tokyo, that runs the b-mobile mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) service, offering low-cost SIM cards and data plans to consumers and, increasingly, communications services for IoT and enterprise customers. It resells network capacity from major operators. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (9424), it is a smaller, niche operator. Consumer-facing in the SIM-only segment, with moderate awareness among price-conscious Japanese users.

Jiashili is a Chinese biscuit and snack food manufacturer based in Kaiping, Guangdong, producing biscuits, cookies, wafers and other bakery snacks sold through supermarkets, convenience stores and distributors across China. It has built its brand around affordable family biscuits and sells through regional distribution networks, with large production plants in Guangdong. It is a listed company, though the exchange is not confirmed here. Consumer snack brand with solid awareness within Guangdong and nearby provinces.

Lakewood-Amedex is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing Bisphosphocin, a new class of anti-infective compounds that kills bacteria and fungi, for wound infections, diabetic foot ulcers and other resistant infections. It is based in Pennsylvania, near the Penn State campus, and was founded to commercialise technology licensed from a university and its inventors. It has no approved products. Listed through the over-the-counter market. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Lixte Biotechnology is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, based in East Setauket, New York, developing LB-100, a small-molecule inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A that is intended to make cancer cells more sensitive to chemotherapy and immunotherapy, tested in ovarian clear cell carcinoma, sarcoma and other tumours. It has no commercial products. Listed on Nasdaq (LIXT) and funded by equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Logistea is a Swedish property company, based in Stockholm, that owns and manages logistics and light industrial properties, mainly in Sweden and neighbouring Nordic markets, leased to tenants such as logistics and manufacturing firms. It grows by acquiring warehouses and distribution centres and earns rental income. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. B2B landlord with no consumer profile and little public brand awareness beyond the property investment community.

Luminex Resources is a Canadian mineral exploration company, based in Vancouver, advancing gold and copper projects in Ecuador, including the Condor gold-copper project in the southeast of the country. The company has no producing mines and is funded by equity raises and project partnerships. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Mineral explorers like this typically sell no products and have to raise funds for each stage of development. B2B mineral explorer with no consumer brand and no sponsorship track record.

Medicus Pharma is a Canadian-US clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in Toronto, developing SkinJect, a doxorubicin-containing dissolvable microneedle patch for the non-surgical treatment of basal cell carcinoma, the most common type of skin cancer, in a Phase 2 trial. It has also pursued other drug-delivery assets. Listed on Nasdaq (MDCX) and the TSX Venture Exchange. No product revenue. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Oncodesign Precision Medicine is a French biotechnology and contract research company, based in Dijon, providing preclinical and translational cancer research services to pharmaceutical firms, while also developing its own drug candidates, including programmes in kinase inhibitors and radiopharmaceuticals. Revenue comes from service contracts and research collaborations with larger drug companies. It is listed on Euronext Paris (ALOPM) and is a small company with a few hundred employees. B2B services firm with no consumer brand profile.

Pentixapharm is a German radiopharmaceutical company, based in Wurzburg, developing diagnostic and therapeutic agents that target the CXCR4 receptor found on certain cancer and cardiovascular disease cells, with a lead imaging agent used for PET scans in conditions such as lymphoma and primary aldosteronism, and therapeutic versions in development. It listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2024. No commercial revenue yet. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

PharmaCorp Rx is a Canadian pharmacy business based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, tagged by Crunchbase under retail and flagged as listed. The data gives no description, but the name and tag point to retail pharmacy operations in Saskatchewan. The number of pharmacies, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available information. Likely a small regional pharmacy brand with local awareness only.
