RenovoRx is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based in Mountain View, California, developing RenovoGem, a product combining its RenovoCath catheter with gemcitabine to deliver chemotherapy directly into the arteries feeding pancreatic tumours, in the Phase 3 TIGeR-PaC trial for locally advanced pancreatic cancer. It has no marketed product and funds operations through equity. Listed on Nasdaq (RNXT). B2B drug and device developer with no consumer profile.

TechFaith Wireless Technology is a Chinese mobile device design house, based in Beijing, that historically designed and developed mobile phones for handset brands and later shifted to IoT, smart devices and other technology businesses. Customers were global and Chinese handset brands and carriers. It listed its American depositary shares on Nasdaq (CNTF) in 2005 and later moved away from its original business. B2B engineering supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Tenon Medical is a US medical device company, based in California, selling the Catamaran SI Joint Fusion System, a minimally invasive implant for treating pain in the sacroiliac joint, to spine and orthopaedic surgeons in the US. Revenue is small and comes from device sales to hospitals and surgery centres. Listed on Nasdaq (TNON) since 2022. B2B medtech with no consumer brand profile.

ZYUS Life Sciences is a Canadian biopharmaceutical company, based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, developing cannabinoid-based drug candidates for pain, neurological and inflammatory conditions, plus some nutraceutical and veterinary products. It grew out of a cannabis-focused business and has research ties to Saskatchewan institutions. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Revenue is small. B2B and development-stage with limited consumer awareness and a modest marketing budget.

Aelis Farma is a French clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, based near Bordeaux, developing a new class of drugs called CB1 signal-specific inhibitors that block the harmful effects of cannabinoid receptor over-activation without affecting normal function. Its lead candidate AEF0117 is being tested for cannabis use disorder, and the company has licensed rights to the drug to Indivior. It also works on cognitive and neurological disorders. Listed on Euronext Paris (AELIS), it has no marketed product and is funded by partner payments and equity. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

AIM ImmunoTech is a US immuno-pharmaceutical company, based in Ocala, Florida, developing Ampligen (rintatolimod), a double-stranded RNA immune modulator, being tested for pancreatic cancer and other solid tumours, with additional interest in viral diseases such as COVID-19 and chronic fatigue syndrome. The company also markets Alferon N (interferon alfa-n3) for genital warts. Listed on NYSE American (AIM), it has minimal revenue and has been through shareholder disputes. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

ALM Equity is a Swedish property developer and owner, based in Sundbyberg near Stockholm, that develops residential and commercial property, mainly for its own long-term holding in the Stockholm area and other Swedish growth regions, leasing apartments and premises and selling projects. It is listed on the Nasdaq First North market in Sweden. Revenue combines rental income and development sales. B2B and tenant-facing property company with no meaningful national consumer brand.

Artelo Biosciences is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, based in La Jolla, California, developing lipid-signalling drugs that modulate the endocannabinoid system. Its lead candidate ART27.13, a cannabinoid receptor agonist that acts mostly outside the brain, is being tested to increase appetite and weight in cancer anorexia-cachexia, and it has other programmes in anxiety and cancer. Listed on Nasdaq (ARTL), it has no commercial product. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

ATM is a Polish data centre and telecom infrastructure operator, based in Warsaw, that runs colocation data centres, including the ATM Ursus campus, and provides cloud, network and IT services to enterprises, banks, public bodies and telecom carriers in Poland and Central Europe. Revenue comes from rack space, power, connectivity and managed services. It is a long-established provider and the Crunchbase record flags it as listed, though ownership has changed over time. B2B infrastructure supplier with little consumer awareness.

Avalon GloboCare is a US-listed healthcare company, based in Freehold, New Jersey, with operations in cell therapy, clinical laboratory services and real estate, historically with links to China. It runs a clinical laboratory services business and pursues cell-based immunotherapy and diagnostic programmes, including collaborations on CAR-T technology, and owns a property in New Jersey. Listed on Nasdaq (AVCO), revenue is small. B2B healthcare company with no consumer brand profile.

Canada Global is an Israeli commercial real estate company based in Herzliya, tagged by Crunchbase under commercial real estate and flagged as listed. Its name suggests a link to Canadian-Israeli property investment, such as the Canada Israel group, but that is an inference. The portfolio, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. Property landlords like this are B2B and have no consumer brand profile. China SXT Pharmaceuticals is a Chinese pharmaceutical company, based in Taizhou, Jiangsu, that makes and sells traditional Chinese medicine products, including prepared slices of Chinese herbal medicine, and related health products, to hospitals, pharmacies and distributors in China. It lists American depositary shares on Nasdaq (SXTC) and has been loss-making with small revenue. B2B and distributor-led, with minimal brand awareness beyond China's herbal medicine trade.

Co-Diagnostics is a US molecular diagnostics company, based in Salt Lake City, that develops and manufactures PCR-based tests using its patented CoPrimer technology, including the Logix Smart COVID-19 test, and tests for tuberculosis and other infectious diseases, and sells a handheld Co-Dx PCR platform for point-of-care use. It sells to laboratories, hospitals and public health programmes in the US, India and other markets. Revenue surged during the pandemic then declined sharply. Listed on Nasdaq (CODX). B2B diagnostics firm with no consumer profile.

Farmmi is a Chinese food company, based in Lishui, Zhejiang, that produces and sells shiitake mushrooms and other edible fungi, in dried, fresh and packaged forms, together with other agricultural products and food items such as health foods. It sells through wholesalers, retailers and online channels in China and exports to Japan, South Korea, the US and Europe. Listed on Nasdaq (FAMI), it has small revenue. B2B and consumer food brand with a modest profile, mostly in China.

GreenFirst Forest Products is a Canadian forest products company, headquartered in North Bay, Ontario, that produces softwood lumber and other wood products at sawmills in Ontario and Quebec, after acquiring Tembec-linked assets from Rayonier Advanced Materials. Customers are lumber wholesalers and home-building suppliers, mainly in North America. Revenue depends on lumber prices and is typically several hundred million dollars. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. B2B commodity producer with no consumer brand profile.

Intelligent Bio Solutions is a medical technology company, with roots in Australia and offices in New York and the UK, that sells the Intelligent Fingerprinting Drug Screening System, a non-invasive test that detects drug use from a fingerprint sweat sample in minutes, used by employers, drug treatment services and in workplaces and the criminal justice sector. Its test cartridges are sold on a consumable basis. Formerly GBS Inc, it is listed on Nasdaq (INBS) and has small revenue. B2B product with little consumer awareness.

Kane Biotech is a Canadian biotechnology company, based in Winnipeg, developing antimicrobial and anti-biofilm technologies for wound care, oral care and animal health, including pet oral-care products and the DispersinB enzyme. It sells products through distributors and licence partners, and revenue is small. Customers are veterinarians, pet owners, healthcare providers and industrial partners. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (KNE). B2B biotech with modest consumer exposure through pet oral-care products.

Lexaria Bioscience is a Canadian and US drug delivery technology company, based in Kelowna, British Columbia, with a patented DehydraTECH technology that improves how fat-soluble active ingredients such as cannabinoids, nicotine and GLP-1 drugs are absorbed in the body. It earns small revenue from licensing and research, and runs early clinical studies of GLP-1 and hypertension drug formulations. Listed on Nasdaq (LEXX). B2B technology licensor with no consumer brand profile.

Liminatus Pharma is a US company with a Wilmington, Delaware, address, tagged by Crunchbase under biopharma, biotechnology and advice, and flagged as listed. No description is provided. It appears to be an early-stage drug company, possibly linked to a SPAC-style listing, but the pipeline, ownership, listing venue and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. Microba Life Sciences is an Australian microbiome company, based in Brisbane, that offers gut microbiome tests and analysis, including the MetaXplore sequencing platform and the Microba Insight test, plus development of live biotherapeutic drugs for conditions such as ulcerative colitis and for supporting cancer immunotherapy. Customers are clinicians, researchers, pharma partners and consumers. It was founded by researchers from the University of Queensland and is listed on the ASX (MAP). Small company with some consumer awareness through gut-health testing.

OKYO Pharma is a UK-incorporated clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, with an office in London, developing treatments for inflammatory eye diseases and pain, led by OK-101, a lipidated chemerin-peptide candidate for neuropathic corneal pain and dry eye disease. It has no marketed product, relies on equity raises and has a very small team. Listed on Nasdaq (OKYO) and previously on the London AIM market. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile and little marketing capacity.

Ondine Biomedical is a Canadian life sciences company, based in Vancouver, that develops photodisinfection technology for killing bacteria, viruses and fungi using light-activated agents, notably the Steriwave nasal photodisinfection system used to reduce surgical site infections by decolonising patients' noses before surgery. It sells to hospitals, mainly in Canada and the UK, and holds regulatory approvals in some markets. Listed on the London AIM market. B2B medical company with no consumer brand profile.

Origin Agritech is a Chinese agricultural biotechnology company, based in Beijing, that breeds, produces and sells hybrid corn seed and other crop seeds, with a focus on genetically modified traits for the Chinese market. It sells to farmers through distributors and has had multi-year operating losses. Listed on Nasdaq (SEED) as a foreign issuer. B2B agricultural supplier with brand recognition among Chinese farmers, but no consumer or global sports-marketing profile.

Ronesans Gayrimenkul Yatirim is a Turkish real estate investment company, based in Istanbul, part of the Ronesans Holding group, that develops and owns shopping malls, office buildings, hotel and residential property, mainly in Turkey. Revenue comes from rent, property sales and project management fees. It is listed on Borsa Istanbul (RGYAS). Part of the Rönesans group, which also builds hospitals and major infrastructure projects worldwide. Consumer-facing through its malls, with modest standalone brand awareness.

Sadot Group is a US agri-commodity trading and food company, based in Burleson, Texas, formerly Muscle Maker Grill, that trades soybeans, corn, wheat and other physical commodities globally and also ran a small restaurant and franchise business. The Sadot Agri-Foods division sources and supplies commodities to processors and food importers, with sizeable revenue but thin margins. Listed on Nasdaq (SDOT). B2B commodity firm, with a legacy burger restaurant brand that gives little consumer awareness.

SenesTech is a US biotechnology company, based in Phoenix, Arizona, that sells ContraPest, a liquid bait that reduces fertility in rats, offered to pest control operators, municipalities and agricultural users as a non-lethal way of reducing rodent populations. Revenue is small, from product sales and some government and commercial contracts, and the company has recorded steady losses. Listed on Nasdaq (SNES). B2B pest-control brand with little consumer recognition.

Sernova is a Canadian clinical-stage biotechnology company, based in London, Ontario, developing the Cell Pouch System, an implantable device that holds therapeutic cells, aimed at treating insulin-dependent diabetes by implanting islet cells, and later other hormone-deficient diseases. It works with partners on stem-cell-derived islet cells. The company has no commercial product and raises equity. Listed on the TSX and the OTC markets (SVA). B2B drug and device developer with no consumer brand profile.

Shuttle Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage specialty pharmaceutical company, based in Rockville, Maryland, developing radiation sensitisers for cancer, led by Ropidoxuridine (IPdR), an oral prodrug of a radiosensitiser in trials for glioblastoma, a deadly brain tumour. The company also works on cancer imaging technology. It has no commercial product, and listed on Nasdaq (SHPH) in 2022. B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Solwers is a Finnish engineering and design consultancy, based in Espoo, with operations across the Nordics and elsewhere in Europe, providing infrastructure, civil and structural engineering, project management and digital design services. Customers are public bodies, property developers and industrial firms. It grew through acquisitions of smaller engineering firms. Listed on Nasdaq First North in Helsinki. B2B professional services firm with little consumer brand awareness.

Sunshine Biopharma is a pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Florida per Crunchbase with its main operations in Montreal, Quebec, selling generic prescription and oncology drugs, nutritional supplements and over-the-counter products through its Nora Pharma subsidiary, which has a large generic portfolio. It also develops anticancer compounds in early research. Listed on Nasdaq (SBFM). Revenue comes from generic drug sales to pharmacies and hospitals in Canada. B2B pharma with limited consumer awareness.

Theralase Technologies is a Canadian medical technology company, based in Toronto, developing light-activated and radiation-activated anti-cancer drugs, known as photo dynamic compounds, with a lead candidate for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, tested with laser light. It also sells therapeutic laser systems for pain relief to chiropractors and clinics, which gives it modest revenue. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TLT). B2B medtech with no major consumer brand profile.

Property companies like this are B2B with no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Vitrafy Life Sciences is an Australian biotechnology company, based in Ballarat, Victoria, that has developed a cryopreservation platform for freezing and storing biological products such as blood, cells and tissues so that they last longer and can be transported more easily, with a focus on blood products. Its customers would be blood banks, hospitals and cell therapy producers. It has no commercial revenue yet and is funded by equity. B2B life science technology firm with no consumer profile.

Unimark Remedies is an Indian healthcare company based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, and flagged as listed. Crunchbase describes it only as a healthcare company, with industry tags of health care and medical, so the product range, such as active pharmaceutical ingredients, formulations or exports, is not confirmed. The Carlsbad Desalination Project is the Claude Bud Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant in San Diego County, California, the largest seawater desalination plant in the Western Hemisphere, developed and owned by Poseidon Water. It produces about 50 million gallons a day of drinking water, roughly 10 percent of the county's supply, under a long-term water purchase agreement with the San Diego County Water Authority. It began operating in 2015 after a long permitting and financing process. A single-asset infrastructure business, B2B with essentially no consumer brand profile.

Bitmain Technologies is a Chinese designer and manufacturer of application-specific integrated circuits for cryptocurrency mining, best known for its Antminer line of bitcoin mining machines, and it also sells AI chips and servers under the Sophon brand. It was founded in 2013 by Jihan Wu and Micree Zhan and is based in Beijing, selling to mining farms and miners worldwide, and it operates the Antpool and BTC.com mining pools. It is one of the largest suppliers of mining hardware, with revenue in the billions of dollars in boom years. Privately held after an unrealised IPO plan. Known in the crypto industry, with limited mainstream consumer awareness.

BRK Ambiental is a Brazilian water and sewage services company, which operates water supply and sewage treatment concessions and public-private partnerships for municipalities across Brazil, and also provides industrial water and effluent treatment services. It serves millions of people in several states. It is controlled by Brookfield Asset Management, which bought it from Odebrecht in 2017. Revenue comes from tariffs and service contracts. Concession-based utility brand known regionally, with local consumer recognition where it operates.

The Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC) is the state-owned operator of Egypt's high-voltage national electricity grid, part of the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company, responsible for transmitting power from generators to distribution companies and for the interconnections with neighbouring countries such as Libya, Jordan and Saudi Arabia. It operates and maintains the 500 kV, 220 kV and lower-voltage network and dispatching centres. Revenue comes from regulated transmission fees. Government-owned B2B monopoly with no consumer brand profile.

GENBAND was a US telecommunications software company, based in Plano, Texas, that supplied IP gateways, session border controllers, voice-over-IP softswitches and unified communications software to telecom operators and enterprises worldwide, including carriers moving to VoIP and 4G voice. It grew from the acquisition of Nortel's carrier voice business in 2010 and was private equity owned. In 2017 it merged with Sonus Networks to form Ribbon Communications, which is listed on Nasdaq. B2B telecom vendor with no consumer brand profile.

HFF was a US commercial real estate capital markets intermediary, based in Dallas, that arranged debt placement, investment sales, equity placement, loan sales and loan servicing for owners of office, multifamily, industrial, retail and hospitality property through offices across the US. Revenue came from transaction fees and servicing. Formerly Holliday Fenoglio Fowler, it listed on the NYSE (HF). In 2019 it was acquired by Jones Lang LaSalle in a deal valued at about 2 billion dollars. B2B advisory firm with little consumer brand profile.

Lytx develops video telematics and fleet safety technology, best known for its DriveCam in-cab event recorders and artificial intelligence that analyses driver behaviour, collisions and risk, to help commercial fleets reduce accidents and insurance costs. Customers include trucking, waste, construction, transit and delivery fleets, paying subscription fees. Based in San Diego, it has hundreds of thousands of vehicles on its platform. It is owned by private equity, Permira acquiring a majority stake in 2018. B2B brand known among fleet managers, but not consumers.

NMC Health was the largest private healthcare operator in the United Arab Emirates, based in Abu Dhabi, running hospitals, clinics, fertility centres and day surgery facilities under the NMC name across the UAE and other markets. Founded by Dr B.R. Shetty, it listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2012 and joined the FTSE 100. In 2020 allegations of hidden debt and fraud led to its collapse and administration, and a long creditor restructuring followed. Once a well-known healthcare brand in the Gulf, it now has a damaged reputation.

Rodnie Polya, which transliterates as Native Fields, is a Russian company based in Rostov, tagged by Crunchbase under agriculture and fleet management, and described as a logistics business that imports and exports goods. The products handled, customers, scale, ownership and any listing cannot be confirmed from the available data. Russian companies also carry sanctions-related risk for international sponsors. It is likely a B2B logistics and agricultural trading firm with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tall City Exploration is a US oil and gas exploration and production company, based in Midland, Texas, backed by the private equity firm Denham Capital. It acquired and developed acreage in the Permian Basin of West Texas, drilling horizontal wells to produce crude oil, natural gas and liquids, and has sold or sought to sell its assets to larger operators. Revenue comes from oil and gas sales. A private B2B energy company with no consumer brand profile.

Cobalt 27 Capital was a Toronto-based metals investment company that held physical cobalt and streams on cobalt-producing mines, such as a stream on the Voisey's Bay mine in Canada, giving investors exposure to the battery metal used in electric vehicle batteries. It was listed in Toronto and later changed ownership. Revenue and value depended on the cobalt price. A financial and resource company with no consumer brand profile.

Greeneden Topco is a Luxembourg holding company that sits at the top of the group behind Genesys, the cloud customer experience and contact centre software provider headquartered in California. Genesys sells omnichannel contact centre, workforce engagement and AI-based customer service software, mainly through its Genesys Cloud platform, to large enterprises worldwide. The group has been owned by private equity firms Hellman and Friedman and Permira. Crunchbase describes Greeneden as being in stealth mode, which is just a holding-company placeholder. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

HCR ManorCare was one of the largest US providers of post-acute and long-term care, operating skilled nursing and rehabilitation centres, assisted living, hospice and home health under the Heartland and ManorCare names, with hundreds of facilities in many states. It was based in Toledo, Ohio, and taken private by the Carlyle Group in 2007 in a deal valued at around 6 billion dollars. Heavy debt and Medicare pressures led it to restructure, and in 2018 its operations were taken over by ProMedica and Welltower. A well-known provider among US seniors and hospitals.

Nyrstar is a global zinc and lead producer, with smelters in Europe, Australia and the Americas, including Budel in the Netherlands, Auby in France, Port Pirie in Australia and Clarksville in the US, and mines in the US. It supplies zinc, lead, silver, indium and germanium to galvanisers and industrial customers, plus its metals processing. Spun off from Umicore and Zinifex in 2007, it was listed in Brussels until a 2019 restructuring handed control to its main creditor and trader Trafigura. B2B metals company with no consumer brand profile.

Pegasus Resources is a US natural resources company, based in Fort Worth, Texas, which Crunchbase describes as a mineral and royalty company. It presumably owns oil and gas mineral and royalty interests, receiving payments from operators, but the acreage, basins, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. Mineral and royalty firms are B2B and have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

RefleXion Medical is a US radiation oncology company, based in Hayward, California, that developed the X1, a radiotherapy system combining a linear accelerator with PET imaging so that the tumour itself guides the radiation beam, known as biology-guided radiotherapy (SCINTIX). It aims to treat tumours that move and metastatic disease, and sells to cancer centres and hospitals. It is venture-backed and received FDA clearances. B2B medical device company with no consumer brand profile.

Tilray Brands is a global cannabis and consumer packaged goods company, listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (TLRY), that grows medical and adult-use cannabis, owns craft beer brands such as SweetWater and Montauk, spirits, hemp foods and wellness products. It operates in Canada, Europe, Australia and the US. It merged with Aphria in 2021, and a significant portion of revenue now comes from alcohol and beverages. It was founded in 2013 and started in Nanaimo, British Columbia. Known consumer brand portfolio, though cannabis advertising is restricted.

Yintai Group is a Chinese retail and real estate investment group founded by Shen Guojun, with its base in Beijing, best known for operating department stores and shopping centres under the Yintai brand across China, including Yintai in77 and Yintai Centre, plus real estate development and financial investments. Alibaba took a stake in Yintai Commerce in 2014. The group has been affected by debt and asset sales. Well-known retail landlord brand in China's major cities, but limited awareness abroad.

Arafura Resources, now called Arafura Rare Earths, is an Australian developer of the Nolans rare earths project in Australia's Northern Territory, planned as a mine and processing hub to produce neodymium-praseodymium oxide used in permanent magnets for electric vehicles and wind turbines. Customers and offtake partners include major battery, magnet and car makers in Asia and Europe, and it has Australian government and export agency support. Based in Perth and listed on the ASX (ARU). It has no producing mine yet. B2B resources developer with no consumer brand profile.

Cell C is South Africa's third-largest mobile network operator, selling prepaid and contract voice, data and handsets to consumers and businesses, and wholesale network access, with a customer base of a few million subscribers. Founded in 2001 and based in Gauteng, it came under the control of Blue Label Telecoms and went through a financial restructuring in 2022 to reduce debt. Cell C is a well-known consumer telecom brand in South Africa, with prominent advertising and past sponsorship of sport.

ConforMIS was a US medical device company, based in Billerica, Massachusetts, that made customised joint replacement implants, including patient-specific knee implants such as iTotal, designed from CT scans of each patient, and also produced instruments and licensed technology. It sold to orthopaedic surgeons and hospitals in the US. It was listed on Nasdaq (CFMS) and in 2023 was acquired by restor3d, a medical device firm, and delisted. B2B medical device company with no consumer brand profile.

Harvest Health and Recreation was a US multistate cannabis operator, based in Tempe, Arizona, that cultivated and sold cannabis products through retail dispensaries across states such as Arizona, Florida, Pennsylvania and Maryland, under the Harvest House of Cannabis and other brands. It was listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and OTC markets. Trulieve acquired it in 2021 in a deal valued at about 2 billion dollars, forming one of the largest US cannabis companies. Cannabis marketing restrictions limit sponsorship use.

Jinjiang Environment is a Chinese waste-to-energy operator, based in Hangzhou, that builds, owns and operates incineration plants converting municipal solid waste into electricity, selling power to the grid and collecting waste treatment fees from local governments. It runs dozens of projects across China, and has also moved into other environmental services and equipment. It is listed in mainland China. B2B and government-focused utility brand, with no consumer awareness.

The Cannabist Company, formerly Columbia Care, is a US multistate cannabis operator, one of the larger ones by revenue, growing and selling medical and adult-use cannabis through its Cannabist retail dispensaries and wholesale brands such as Seed and Strain and Triple Seven in states including New York, New Jersey, Illinois, Virginia and Massachusetts. It is listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and OTC markets. Revenue is in the hundreds of millions of dollars, with a leveraged balance sheet. Cannabis advertising restrictions limit conventional sponsorship.

US Acute Care Solutions (USACS) is a large physician-owned emergency medicine and acute care group, headquartered in Canton, Ohio, that staffs hospital emergency departments and provides hospital medicine, observation and telemedicine services across many US states, with thousands of clinicians. Hospitals contract with USACS to run their emergency services, and the group is governed by its physician partners, rather than outside investors. B2B healthcare staffing brand, known to hospital administrators but not to the public.

Voodoo is a French mobile games publisher and developer, based in Paris, known for hyper-casual and casual titles such as Hole.io, Paper.io, Mob Control and Helix Jump, which are free to play and earn revenue from in-app advertising and purchases. Founded in 2013 by Alexandre Yazdi, it has been downloaded billions of times and has become one of the largest mobile publishers worldwide. Tencent took a minority stake in 2021, and Voodoo bought the social app BeReal in 2024. Large reach among mobile players but few players know the company name.

Arrail Dental is a Chinese private dental clinic chain, based in Beijing, offering general dentistry, orthodontics, implants and paediatric dental care to urban consumers through a network of clinics in major cities, as one of the better-known private dental chains. It sells services directly to patients, with average treatment prices well above public hospitals. The chain has been backed by private investors and is flagged here as listed. Consumer-facing healthcare brand in China.

Calgon Carbon, whose Crunchbase fields were corrupted in the screen recording, is a US company known as a global producer of activated carbon and related water and air treatment equipment, based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It was listed on the NYSE (CCC) before the Japanese chemical group Kuraray acquired it in 2018 for about 1.1 billion dollars. B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer awareness.

Danimer Scientific was a US bioplastics company, based in Bainbridge, Georgia, that produced Nodax PHA, a biodegradable plastic made by fermentation from vegetable oils, for use in items such as straws, coffee pods, packaging and cutlery, and sold to consumer brand and packaging customers. It listed via a SPAC merger in 2020 on the NYSE (DNMR), and struggled with losses and debt. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2025. B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand, though it had links to major beverage and food brands.

Harte Gold is a Canadian gold mining company, based in Toronto, which owns and operated the Sugar Zone mine near White River, Ontario, producing gold from an underground mine and mill. It struggled with operational problems and debt, went through creditor protection and its lenders ended up with the asset. It was listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange. B2B resource company with no consumer brand and little capacity for sponsorship.

Matterport is a US spatial data company, based in Sunnyvale, California, that makes cameras and cloud software to capture buildings and turn them into immersive 3D digital twins, used for real estate listings, facilities management, insurance, retail and construction. Customers are real estate agents, property companies, enterprises and consumers, paying subscription fees. It listed on Nasdaq (MTTR) in 2021 through a SPAC merger and was acquired by CoStar Group in 2025. Well known in property marketing circles, with a growing brand.

Meizhong Jiahe Hospital Management is a Chinese hospital management company based in Haidian, Beijing, tagged by Crunchbase under health care and hospitals and flagged as listed. VWR is a global supplier of laboratory products, chemicals, consumables, equipment and services to science, health and industry, selling through catalogues, e-commerce and a field sales force to pharmaceutical, biotech, hospital, university and industrial laboratories worldwide. B2B brand with strong recognition among laboratory scientists but not the general public.

Beijing OriginWater Technology is a Chinese water treatment and environmental company that designs, builds and operates sewage treatment, drinking water, membrane and wastewater reuse plants, along with water-environment restoration and industrial wastewater projects. Customers are local governments, industrial parks and industrial companies, and revenue comes from project construction contracts and operation fees. Founded in 2001, based in Beijing, it is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. B2B and government-focused, with no consumer brand awareness.

CarbonFree Technology is described by Crunchbase as a recognised leader in a technology area, with the text cut off, and tagged under carbon capture and project management with a Toronto base. The products, customers, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. B2B cleantech firms like this usually have no consumer brand profile. Clarify Health Solutions is a US healthcare analytics company, based in San Francisco, that provides a cloud platform using claims data and AI to analyse patient outcomes, costs and care patterns, helping health plans, provider groups, life sciences firms and government agencies with value-based care, risk and benchmarking decisions. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and analytics services. Founded around 2017, it is venture backed. B2B health technology brand known in healthcare analytics, with no consumer profile.

Crossroads Impact Corp, formerly Crossroads Systems, is a Dallas-based financial services holding company that owns Capital Plus Financial, a US community development financial institution (CDFI) lending to small businesses, mortgage borrowers and low-income communities. It became a significant Paycheck Protection Program lender during 2020 and 2021. Its Crunchbase description refers to a global provider of customer service solutions, which looks like a mismatched entry. It is listed on the OTC markets (CRSS). B2B and community lending brand with local rather than national awareness.

Cyara is a customer experience assurance software company that automates testing and monitoring of contact centres, chatbots, voice systems and digital channels, to ensure that customer journeys work correctly. Customers are large enterprises, including banks, telecom operators and retailers. Founded in Melbourne, Australia, in 2006 and now headquartered in Redwood City, California, it raised significant funding including a large growth investment from Vista Equity Partners in 2022. B2B software firm with no consumer brand profile.

Eargo is a US hearing aid company, based in San Jose, California, that sold nearly invisible, rechargeable over-the-counter-style hearing aids directly to consumers online and by telephone, and became known for its marketing in the pre-pandemic years. It listed on Nasdaq (EAR) in 2020, was subject to a US Department of Justice insurance billing investigation in 2021, and was taken private in 2024 by Patient Square Capital. Customers are adults with mild to moderate hearing loss. Consumer brand with strong digital marketing.

EndoGastric Solutions is a US medical device company, based in Redmond, Washington, that makes the EsophyX device and the Transoral Incisionless Fundoplication (TIF) procedure, a minimally invasive treatment for chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease, which avoids open surgery. It sells to hospitals and gastroenterology and surgery teams, and reimbursement from insurers helps adoption. Privately held and venture backed. B2B medical device company, known among gastroenterologists and surgeons, with no consumer brand profile.

Everside Health is a US direct primary care provider, based in Denver, that runs employer-sponsored and union-sponsored health centres and virtual care, offering primary care, behavioural health, physical therapy and pharmacy services to employees and their families, in return for membership fees paid by employers. It operates hundreds of clinics across many US states. It was formed through a combination of Paladina Health and Activate Healthcare. B2B health provider with limited consumer brand awareness.

JenaValve Technology is a US-German medical device company, headquartered in Irvine, California, that develops transcatheter heart valve systems, notably the Trilogy valve for aortic regurgitation and stenosis, implanted without open-heart surgery. Customers are hospitals and cardiac surgery and cardiology teams. Edwards Lifesciences announced a plan to acquire it in 2024, which US antitrust authorities later challenged. Venture backed. B2B medical device firm with no consumer brand profile.

Karora Resources was a Canadian gold and nickel mining company, based in Toronto, whose main asset was the Beta Hunt mine in Western Australia, which produced gold and nickel, and a nearby Higginsville operation with a gold processing plant. It sold gold to refiners and nickel to smelters. It was listed on the TSX and in 2024 was acquired by Gold Fields in a deal valued at around 1.6 billion Canadian dollars. B2B resource company with no consumer brand profile.

MindMaze Group (Legacy) is a Swiss neurotechnology company, originally based in Lausanne, known for digital therapeutics and virtual-reality-based rehabilitation for stroke and brain injury patients, using products such as MindMotion and its brain-computer interface research. Customers are hospitals, rehabilitation centres and health systems. The company was founded in 2012 by Tej Tadi and raised large venture rounds. The legacy label suggests the original group has been restructured or merged, so the current structure should be checked. B2B medtech with no consumer brand profile.

Sabina Gold and Silver was a Canadian gold development company, based in Vancouver, which owned the Back River gold project in Nunavut, in Canada's Arctic, comprising the Goose and George deposits, and was building the Goose mine. It had financing arrangements with lenders and royalty partners and was listed on the TSX. B2Gold completed its acquisition of Sabina in 2023 for roughly 1 billion Canadian dollars, so it no longer exists as an independent company. Resource firm with no consumer brand profile.

Solek is a Czech-headquartered renewable energy company, based in Prague, that develops, builds and operates photovoltaic solar power plants, with activity in the Czech Republic, Chile, Poland and other markets. It sells electricity and construction services to investors and utilities. The Crunchbase record flags it as listed, but the exchange is not confirmed here. B2B energy developer, with limited consumer brand profile.

Source Global, known as SOURCE, is a US cleantech company, based in Scottsdale, Arizona, that makes SOURCE Hydropanels, solar-powered panels that extract drinking water from air without a grid connection, with a focus on remote homes, schools, farms and commercial buildings, and runs water-as-a-service installations. It was founded as Zero Mass Water by Cody Friesen of Arizona State University. Customers are households, institutions, governments and developers across dozens of countries. Venture backed. Mission-led consumer and institutional brand with moderate awareness.

Vitrolife is a Swedish medical technology and life sciences company, based in Gothenburg, that supplies products used in fertility treatment (IVF), such as culture media, instruments, time-lapse embryo imaging systems and genetic testing services, together with transplantation products. Customers are fertility clinics and hospitals in more than a hundred countries. Revenue is in the billions of Swedish kronor. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (VITR). B2B brand known to embryologists and fertility clinics, but not to the public.

Bioneb is a London-based company that Crunchbase tags under biotechnology and genetics, with a description about offering direct-to-consumer genetic testing. Genetic testing providers sell to consumers online, but nothing here shows a known brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Equashield is a US-headquartered medical device company, based in Port Washington, New York, that makes closed-system drug transfer devices (CSTDs) and robotic compounding systems for safe handling of hazardous drugs such as chemotherapy, protecting pharmacists and nurses from exposure. It sells to hospitals, cancer centres and pharmacies in North America, Europe and elsewhere. Privately held. B2B healthcare supplier, known among oncology pharmacists, with no consumer profile.

Expel is a US cybersecurity company, based in Herndon, Virginia, providing managed detection and response (MDR) services, with its Expel Workbench platform and analysts monitoring customers' cloud, network and endpoint security tools, and triaging alerts for them. Customers are mid-sized and large enterprises that outsource security operations, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2016 by security industry veterans, it is venture backed. B2B security brand known in the cybersecurity market, with no consumer profile.

Friday Health Plans was a US health insurer, based in Denver, selling individual and family plans, mostly on the Affordable Care Act marketplace in states including Texas, Colorado, Florida and Georgia, with low-priced offerings and a digital-first, simplified-enrolment pitch. It grew quickly in 2021 and 2022, with venture backing, then ran into financial trouble and regulatory action and was closed down in 2023, leaving members to move to other plans. Once a visible consumer insurance brand in its states.

Fullerton Health is a Singapore-based healthcare group, offering occupational health, general practice, specialist care, allied health, dental and corporate healthcare services through a network of clinics and corporate health contracts in Singapore and other Asia-Pacific markets. Customers are employers, insurers and individuals. It is owned by Fullerton Healthcare Corporation, which has links to Temasek. Widely known in Singapore for corporate and employer healthcare, with moderate consumer awareness.

Gordon Brothers is a global advisory, restructuring and investment firm, based in Boston, that helps retailers and lenders value, sell and finance assets, through brands including liquidation and store-closing services, asset appraisal, brand licensing and acquisition, and lending based on inventory and other assets. Customers are retailers, banks and companies in distress, and revenue comes from fees and investment returns. Founded in 1903, it handled the liquidation of well-known retail chains. Privately held B2B brand known in retail finance circles, with little consumer profile.

Invacare is a US medical equipment manufacturer, based in Elyria, Ohio, making wheelchairs, power mobility devices, home oxygen concentrators, beds and other home medical equipment used by seniors and people with disabilities, sold through distributors and providers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific. It was listed on the NYSE (IVC) and restructured through Chapter 11 in 2023, becoming a private company. B2B healthcare brand known to care providers and wheelchair users, but not heavily advertised to consumers.

Leia Inc. is a US display technology company, based in Menlo Park, California, which develops lightfield displays that show 3D images without special glasses, based on Leia's lightfield technology. Its products have included the Lume Pad tablet, 3D phone displays licensed to handset makers and displays for professional markets. Customers are device makers, content creators and enterprises. It spun out of HP Labs research, is venture backed, and has a small team. B2B display technology licensor, with modest consumer awareness.

Siegfried Rhein is a Mexican pharmaceutical company, based in Mexico City, that develops, makes and sells prescription medicines, generics and consumer health products in Mexico and wider Latin America. Customers are pharmacies, hospitals, doctors and distributors. The name reflects its historical links to the Swiss pharmaceutical group Siegfried. B2B pharma brand with some consumer-facing over-the-counter products, and moderate recognition within Mexico.

Yubico is a Swedish cybersecurity hardware company, based in Stockholm, which makes the YubiKey, a small hardware security key that protects online accounts from phishing using strong two-factor and passwordless login standards such as FIDO2, and used by consumers, enterprises, governments and tech companies, including Google and Microsoft. Revenue comes from key sales and enterprise subscriptions. Founded in 2007 by Stina Ehrensvard and Jakob Ehrensvard, it is listed on Nasdaq First North Premier Growth Market (YUBICO) and has hundreds of employees. Strong brand among security professionals, with growing mainstream awareness.

Allm Inc. is a Japanese medical ICT company, based in Tokyo, that provides cloud-based medical information and remote medicine services, including systems for video consultations, cloud-based electronic medical records and imaging, and telemedicine tools for hospitals, clinics and care providers. It sells software and service subscriptions to medical institutions. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. B2B healthcare technology brand known among Japanese clinics, with no consumer profile.

ASG Eye Hospital is an Indian chain of super-specialty eye hospitals, based in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, providing cataract surgery, LASIK, retina, glaucoma, cornea and paediatric eye care through a growing network of hospitals and clinics across many Indian states. Patients pay for treatment directly or through insurance and government schemes. Known to patients in its regions through local advertising, with moderate consumer awareness in India.

Exer Urgent Care is a US urgent care operator, based in El Segundo, California, running clinics in the Los Angeles area that offer walk-in and online-booked care for minor illness and injury, plus occupational health and primary care, with an emphasis on convenience. Revenue comes from patient visits and insurance payments. Local consumer brand in Southern California, with modest awareness and a small footprint compared with national urgent care chains.

Medically Home was a US healthcare technology company, based in Boston, that enabled hospital-level care in patients' homes, combining a technology platform, remote monitoring, logistics, pharmacy and a clinical command centre with health system partners such as Mass General Brigham and Atrium Health. Revenue came from partner health systems and payers. It merged with DispatchHealth in 2023 to create a large home-based care company. B2B health platform with little consumer brand profile.

Quartet Health is a US behavioural health technology company, based in New York, whose platform helps primary care doctors, health plans and employers identify patients needing mental health care and connect them with therapists and psychiatrists, supporting collaborative care. Customers include health plans, health systems and employers, paying for platform and services. Founded in 2014, it raised substantial venture funding from investors including Oak HC/FT and General Catalyst. B2B health technology brand with no consumer profile.

RWDC Industries is a bioplastics company, based in Athens, Georgia, with operations in Singapore, that developed PHA-based biodegradable materials under the Solon brand, such as drinking straws and cutlery produced from fermentation of plant oils, aimed at replacing single-use petroleum-based plastics. Customers are food service brands, packaging companies and consumer product makers. Venture backed with investor support. B2B materials supplier with no consumer profile, although its straws were used by some restaurant and retail chains.

Swiss Medical Network is the largest private hospital group in Switzerland, based in Genolier, operating dozens of private clinics and hospitals in French-, German- and Italian-speaking regions, with specialist care in surgery, orthopaedics, oncology, maternity and emergency services. It is a subsidiary of the listed Aevis Victoria group, with outside investors holding minority stakes. Patients are privately insured or self-paying. Known healthcare brand within Switzerland, with moderate consumer awareness.

AltraBiofuels is a US cleantech company with an Omaha, Nebraska, address in the data, which Crunchbase describes as a producer of renewable fuels. Its tags cover biofuel, fuel and information technology. The facilities, capacity, ownership and current status cannot be confirmed from the available data, and the company may no longer be operating. B2B fuel producer with no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Bang Er Orthopedic is a healthcare company based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China, tagged by Crunchbase under health care and medical, and described as a Hangzhou-based healthcare business. Chinese orthopaedic care providers are mostly regional brands without international profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Battlecat Oil and Gas is a private US energy company, based in Houston, Texas, that focuses on acquiring and developing oil and gas assets, according to Crunchbase, with tags for energy, oil and gas, and services. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

BlueArc was a US data storage company, based in San Jose, California, that built high-performance network attached storage (NAS) and unified storage systems, including the Titan and Mercury series, for use in demanding sectors such as media, oil and gas exploration, life sciences and education. Customers were large enterprises and research institutions. It was acquired by Hitachi Data Systems in 2011, and its technology became part of Hitachi's NAS portfolio. B2B enterprise storage brand with no consumer profile.

Bond Vet is a US veterinary clinic chain, based in New York, running design-forward neighbourhood pet clinics with primary care, urgent care, wellness plans and an app, in cities including New York, Boston, Philadelphia and Washington DC. It positions itself as a modern, friendlier alternative to traditional vet practices. Revenue comes from clinic visits and membership plans. Founded in 2016, it is venture backed. Consumer brand with strong local awareness among pet owners in its cities and heavy social media presence.

Cadence Bank is a US regional bank formed in 2021 from the merger of BancorpSouth and Cadence Bancorporation, headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi, with offices in Houston, and a large branch network across the South, offering commercial banking, consumer banking, mortgages, wealth management and insurance, with assets of roughly 45 to 50 billion dollars. It is listed on the NYSE (CADE). Customers are businesses and individuals across states such as Mississippi, Texas, Alabama, Tennessee and Florida. Regional brand with strong local awareness and community sponsorship activity.

CRT Capital Group was a US institutional securities broker-dealer, based in Darien, Connecticut, specialising in fixed income, credit and convertible securities research, sales and trading for hedge funds and institutional investors, and also offered investment banking and restructuring advice. It was an independent firm that was later sold or merged into larger groups. Revenue came from trading commissions and advisory fees. B2B financial brand known in credit markets, with no consumer profile.

eSolar was a US concentrating solar power company, based in Pasadena, California, backed by the Idealab incubator, that developed modular solar tower technology using many small mirrors (heliostats) focused on a central receiver to make steam and electricity for utilities. It built the Sierra SunTower demonstration plant in California and planned projects in the US, India and China. Babcock and Wilcox acquired its technology in 2014. B2B energy technology firm with no consumer brand profile.

GenesisCare is an international cancer care and radiation therapy provider, founded in Australia and based in Sydney, operating oncology centres, radiation therapy facilities, cardiology and urology clinics in Australia, the UK, Spain and the US. Revenue comes from patient treatments paid by insurers, public health systems and patients. Backed by private equity investors and the Chinese conglomerate Fosun, it had big debts and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 2024, after which parts of the business were sold. Known healthcare brand in Australia, with reputational damage from its financial collapse.

HydroChile is a clean energy company based in Melbourne, Australia, whose Crunchbase description says it builds and operates hydroelectric power stations. The name points to hydropower projects in Chile, but the projects, capacity, ownership and listing details cannot be confirmed from the available data. Hydroelectric developers sell power to utilities and have no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

JinkoSolar is a leading Chinese solar panel manufacturer, headquartered in Shanghai, with large factories in China, Malaysia, Vietnam and the US, and one of the world's largest shippers of photovoltaic modules, selling its Tiger series of high-efficiency panels to utilities, project developers, distributors and installers in over 100 countries. It is vertically integrated from ingots and wafers to cells and modules, with annual revenue of tens of billions of dollars. Listed on the NYSE (JKS) and Shanghai STAR Market. Large B2B brand that has used sports sponsorship.

Kerasotes Theatres was a US movie theatre chain, based in Chicago, that operated ShowPlace and other cinemas across the Midwest, and traced its origins to a single storefront nickelodeon in 1909. It was a family business that grew into one of the larger regional circuits, with dozens of multiplexes and 3D screens. The chain was later sold to new owners and no longer operates as a standalone company. Consumer-facing local cinema brand in its Midwest markets, now historic.

Marathon Gold was a Canadian gold development company, based in Toronto, building the Valentine Gold Project in central Newfoundland, the largest undeveloped gold project in Atlantic Canada, with several open pits and a mill planned. It had financing arrangements with banks and royalty partners, and was listed on the TSX. Calibre Mining acquired it in 2024, so it no longer exists as an independent company. B2B resource company with no consumer brand profile.

Nel Hydrogen, now listed as Nel ASA, is a Norwegian company, headquartered in Oslo, that makes electrolysers to produce green hydrogen from water and renewable power, and hydrogen fuelling stations. It manufactures alkaline and PEM electrolysers in Norway, Denmark and the US, selling to energy companies, industrial firms and project developers. The company is a pioneer in hydrogen with over 90 years of electrolyser history. Listed on Euronext Oslo (NEL). B2B energy-transition brand, known in the hydrogen industry and among investors, with little consumer profile.

NeoPhotonics was a US maker of optical networking components, based in San Jose, California, producing high-speed lasers, optical modules, coherent transceivers and photonic integrated circuits for telecom, data centre and cable networks, with plants in China and Japan. Customers were network equipment makers and cloud operators. It was listed on the NYSE (NPTN) and in 2022 was acquired by Lumentum for about 918 million dollars. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Picturehouse Media is an Indian film production and media company, based in Hyderabad, and a subsidiary of the PVP Global Ventures group. It produces and distributes Telugu, Tamil and other regional language films and has had a presence in film distribution and exhibition-related media. Revenue comes from film rights and distribution. It is a privately held arm of a larger group. Regional film brand with moderate recognition in the south Indian film industry.

SCM Insurance Services is a Canadian company, based in Edmonton, Alberta, that Crunchbase describes as offering a suite of insurance-related services, with tags for financial services and information technology. The specific business, such as claims management, ownership, scale and listing status cannot be confirmed from the available data. It is probably a B2B insurance services provider with no consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

SI-BONE is a US medical device company, based in Santa Clara, California, which makes the iFuse family of titanium implants for sacroiliac joint dysfunction and the iFuse-3D and Granite systems for pelvic fixation and spine surgery, sold to spine and orthopaedic surgeons and hospitals in the US and Europe. It was founded in 2008 and is listed on Nasdaq (SIBN) with annual revenue of well over 100 million dollars. Reimbursement by US insurers supports demand. B2B medtech with no consumer profile.

SquareTrade was a US consumer electronics and appliance protection company, based in San Francisco, which sold extended warranties and protection plans for phones, laptops, TVs, appliances and other devices through retailers such as Walmart, Costco and Amazon and direct to consumers, with claims handled through its own service network. It was founded in 1999 and was acquired by Allstate in 2016 for about 1.4 billion dollars. Became part of Allstate Protection Plans. Consumer-facing brand with sizeable retail visibility.

Tacora Resources is a Canadian iron ore producer, based in Newfoundland and Labrador, which owns and operates the Scully Mine near Wabush and produces high-grade iron ore concentrate for steelmakers in Europe, Asia and North America. It was formed in 2017 through acquisition of the Scully mine and, as a private company backed by Cargill and others, went through debt restructuring in the 2020s. B2B mining firm with no consumer brand profile.

Vubiquity was a US content services company, based in Burbank, California, that supplied multi-platform video distribution services to studios, broadcasters and pay TV operators, including content aggregation, encoding, localisation and video on demand delivery, serving customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia. The business was acquired by Amdocs in 2018 and absorbed into its media operations. B2B media services supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Accela is a US software company, based in San Ramon, California, selling cloud-based software to local governments for permitting, licensing, code enforcement, planning, land management and civic engagement, used by cities, counties and states across the US and in several other countries. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and services. It is privately held and has had private equity ownership. B2B government technology brand, known to public sector administrators and contractors, with no consumer profile.
